Design Document (GDD/PRD)

▼

1.0 Project Overview

▼

Solar System Coop is a single-player, wave-based survival defense game developed in Unity for Android. The project serves as a foundational "passion project" for a solo developer to master core game development mechanics, including spawning systems, hitboxes, automated targeting logic, and complex data-driven economies. While launching as a single-player experience (MVP), the architecture is designed to support future cooperative multiplayer and expanded mechanical depth.

2.0 Core Gameplay Loop

▼

The game takes place on a single-lane, fixed-map interface.

  • Defensive Position: The player’s ship is stationed at the "close end" (bottom/side) of the screen.
  • Enemy Approach: Enemies spawn at the "far end" and move in a direct, straight line toward the player’s ship to inflict damage.
  • Automated Combat: Weapon fire and targeting are fully automated. Strategic depth is derived from ship selection, weapon loadouts, and upgrade paths rather than manual aiming.
  • Wave Structure: Enemies arrive in progressively difficult waves. Between waves, players access a shop/upgrade menu to refine their "firewall" of weaponry.
  • Death & Revival: Upon ship destruction, players are presented with a choice to restart or utilize a "Second Chance" mechanic via rewarded advertisements.

3.0 Ship & Weapon Mechanics

▼

Ship Systems

  • Slots: Ships are defined by the number of available weapon slots.
  • Progression: Players start with a basic ship (1 slot). New ship models with more slots or unique intrinsic abilities are unlocked via XP and wave milestones.
  • Premium Options: High-tier ship designs with unique aesthetic profiles and specialized stats are available via In-App Purchases (IAP).
  • Customization: Players choose which weapons to slot into their ship, creating a tailored defensive strategy.

Weaponry & Targeting

Weapons possess specialized automated targeting logic, including:

  • Closest Proximity: Targets the nearest threat.
  • Type-Specific: Targets ground vs. air units.
  • AOE (Area of Effect): Targets clusters/groupings of enemies.
  • Priority-Based: Targets Bosses before minions, or vice versa.
  • Durability (Future-Proofing): Weapons will eventually feature a durability stat. If it reaches zero, the weapon becomes invalid. Players must choose to repair or replace it at a cost.

4.0 Economy & Data Matrices

▼

The project relies on a robust "Economy Matrix" (implemented via ScriptableObjects or 2D arrays) to manage scaling, balance, and monetization hooks.

A. Combat Effectiveness Matrix (Elemental Rock-Paper-Scissors)

A 2D float array handles multipliers between DamageType and ResistanceType:

  • Fire: 1.5x vs. Bio/Organic; 0.5x vs. Water.
  • Water: 1.5x vs. Fire/Electric; 0.5x vs. Bio.
  • Electric: Bonus vs. Shields/Water; Resisted by Kinetic/Heavy Armor.
  • Kinetic: 1.0x (Standard) across all types.

B. Progression & Upgrade Matrix

  • Stair-Step Model: Designed for a sense of accomplishment every 15–20 minutes.
  • Currency Multipliers: Integrated hooks for "Double Earnings" rewards to accelerate progression.
  • Ship Unlocks: First ship upgrade at Wave 5 (End of intro phase).
  • Weapon Unlocks: First new weapon at Wave 2; new types every 3–5 waves.
  • Tech Tiers:
    • Tier 1 (Waves 1-10): Basic weapons, low-cost upgrades.
    • Tier 2 (Waves 11-25): Elemental/AOE weapons, exponential cost scaling.

C. Enemy Compendium Matrix

Tracks enemy stats including HP, Shield values, Special Abilities, and Movement speed.

5.0 Technical Implementation (Unity)

▼
  • Physics: Simple hitboxes and triggers for collision detection.
  • Architecture: Use of Enums for Damage/Resistance types to allow for easy expansion.
  • Monetization Integration:
    • Unity Ads SDK: Implementation of Rewarded Video Ad placements at key game states.
    • Unity IAP: Secure integration for the $1.99 premium ship storefront.
  • State Management: Clear separation between "Combat State," "Upgrade State," and "Monetization/Ad State."

6.0 Monetization Strategy

▼

The game utilizes a hybrid monetization model designed to support ongoing development while maintaining a fair player experience.

  • Rewarded Advertisements (Unity Ads SDK):
    • Revive Mechanic: Upon ship death, players can watch an ad to revive with 50% health and continue their current run.
    • Currency Booster: At the "Wave Complete" stage, players can opt to watch an ad to double the currency earned during that wave.
  • In-App Purchases (IAP):
    • Premium Ship Designs: Exclusive ship models featuring unique visuals and competitive stats available for a flat fee of $1.99.
  • Sustainability: Revenue generated will be reinvested into post-release updates, server costs for future co-op, and professional asset acquisition.

7.0 Roadmap & MVP Goals

▼
  • MVP Status: Single-player only, core wave loop, basic economy matrices, and functional ship/weapon unlocking.
  • Monetization Launch: Integration of the Unity Ads SDK and the initial IAP ship storefront.
  • Post-Launch:
    • Co-op multiplayer integration.
    • Implementation of the Durability/Repair system.
    • Visual overhaul using professional assets.

8.0 Success Criteria

▼

Each development task (AI spawning, ad-trigger logic, IAP verification, etc.) must meet specific Acceptance Criteria to ensure the mechanic is functional and the developer has mastered the underlying Unity concept before moving to the next feature.

Pitch Deck

▼

SLIDE 1: Title Slide

Solar System Coop

A Strategic, Automated Defense Experience for Android.

SLIDE 2: The Problem

The mobile defense market is saturated with complex, manual-control games. There is a clear desire for a focused, strategic experience that respects the player's time, offering deep engagement without demanding constant, intricate input. Players seek meaningful decisions in a streamlined, accessible format.

SLIDE 3: The Solution: Your Project

Solar System Coop is a single-player, wave-based survival defense game for Android that redefines strategic depth through automated combat and a dynamic economy. It offers a focused, satisfying experience for players who want to make impactful decisions without the burden of constant manual control.

SLIDE 4: Core Features & Loop

Players defend a single lane against waves of enemies by strategically selecting and upgrading their automated ship. The core loop involves:

  • Automated Combat: Focus on strategic choices, not manual aiming.
  • Dynamic Ship & Weapon System: Unlock new ships with unique abilities and customize weapon loadouts (e.g., closest, AOE, type-specific).
  • Deep Economy & Progression: A robust matrix governs weapon effectiveness (elemental rock-paper-scissors), enemy stats, and player progression, with significant upgrades available every 15-20 minutes.
  • Strategic Depth: Decisions on ship choice, weapon loadouts, and upgrade paths are crucial for survival against increasingly difficult waves.

SLIDE 5: Unique Selling Proposition

Solar System Coop differentiates itself through:

  • Focus on Strategic Decision-Making: Unlike many manual-control games, our depth lies in high-level choices (what to upgrade, what to equip) rather than micro-management.
  • Automated Combat: Provides a unique, time-respectful experience that is accessible yet engaging.
  • Robust, Data-Driven Economy: A well-defined matrix for weapon, enemy, and progression stats ensures a balanced and scalable challenge.
  • Future-Proof Architecture: Designed from the ground up to support future co-op multiplayer and expanded content.

SLIDE 6: Target Audience

Our target audience is casual to mid-core mobile gamers who enjoy strategy, tower defense, and survival genres but are seeking a more focused, time-efficient experience. This includes:

  • Players who enjoy strategic depth but have limited time for complex controls.
  • Fans of automated combat and idle-style progression.
  • A market of millions of Android users seeking engaging, single-player defense challenges.

SLIDE 7: Art & Style

The visual style is a clean, modern, and vibrant sci-fi aesthetic. The design will focus on clear, readable UI and distinct, easily identifiable ship and enemy models. The initial MVP will use placeholder assets, with a plan to replace them with high-quality, professional 2D or 3D assets post-launch to enhance the game's appeal and marketability.

SLIDE 8: The Team

This project is driven by a single, dedicated solo developer with a strong foundation in game architecture and a passion for creating engaging, strategic experiences. The developer has expertise in Unity, C#, and the core principles of game balancing and data management. The focus is on building a solid, functional foundation that can be expanded upon.

SLIDE 9: The Ask & Roadmap

We are seeking a partnership to bring Solar System Coop to a wider audience and support its post-launch development. Our roadmap includes:

  • MVP Completion: Launching the single-player version with core features and a free-to-play, donation-supported model.
  • Monetization Integration: Implementing a rewarded ad system for in-game revives and currency boosts, and a one-time IAP for a unique ship cosmetic ($1.99).
  • Post-Launch Updates: Developing and releasing co-op multiplayer, new ships, weapons, and content based on player feedback and market performance.
  • Timeline: MVP launch within 6 months, with the first major content update (Co-op) targeted for 3 months post-launch.

MVP Definition

▼

Summary

This document outlines the Minimum Viable Product (MVP) for 'Solar System Coop', a single-player, wave-based survival defense game. The MVP will focus on establishing the core gameplay loop, a basic economy, and the initial monetization strategy. Key features include automated combat, wave progression, a two-tiered progression system, and the integration of Unity Ads for a revive mechanic and currency doubling, alongside a $1.99 In-App Purchase for a new ship design. The architecture is being built with future co-op multiplayer and additional features in mind.

In Scope

  • ✓ Single-player core wave-based survival gameplay loop.
  • ✓ Automated ship targeting and combat.
  • ✓ Wave progression with increasing difficulty.
  • ✓ Basic economy with currency for upgrades and unlocks.
  • ✓ Ship and weapon unlocking via progression milestones (Wave 5 for first upgrade).
  • ✓ Integration of Unity Ads SDK for Rewarded Video Ads.
  • ✓ Rewarded Ad placement upon ship death for a 50% health revive.
  • ✓ Rewarded Ad placement at Wave Complete to double currency earned.
  • ✓ Integration of Unity IAP for a single $1.99 premium ship with unique stats and visuals.
  • ✓ Implementation of the Combat Effectiveness (Rock-Paper-Scissors) matrix.
  • ✓ Implementation of the Progression & Upgrade Matrix for the first tier.
  • ✓ Basic Enemy Compendium data structure.
  • ✓ Core state management for Combat, Upgrade, and Monetization states.
  • ✓ Initial setup for future co-op multiplayer architecture.

Out of Scope

  • ✕ Cooperative multiplayer functionality.
  • ✕ Implementation of the Ship Durability and Repair system.
  • ✕ Additional premium ship designs beyond the initial one.
  • ✕ More complex monetization models (e.g., subscriptions, bundles).
  • ✕ Advanced enemy types with unique AI behaviors.
  • ✕ Full visual overhaul with professional assets (planned post-launch).
  • ✕ Server infrastructure for future multiplayer.
  • ✕ A/B testing of monetization strategies.
  • ✕ Integration with third-party analytics platforms.

Technical Specifications

TS-001: Monetization Strategy & Implementation

This document details the monetization plan for 'Solar System Coop', integrating Unity Ads and In-App Purchases (IAP) to create a sustainable revenue stream.

1. Overview

The monetization strategy is designed to enhance player experience and provide value, rather than acting as a barrier to core gameplay. It focuses on optional, rewarded video ads and a single, affordable premium content purchase.

2. Monetization Features

2.1. Rewarded Video Ads (Unity Ads)

Rewarded ads will be integrated at key moments to provide players with strategic advantages and rewards, encouraging engagement and offering a free path to progression.

2.1.1. Revive Mechanic (US-001)

  • Trigger: Upon player ship's health reaching 0% (death).
  • Player Action: The player is presented with an option to watch a rewarded video ad.
  • Reward: Upon successful completion of the ad, the player's ship health is restored to 50%. The game state transitions back to the current wave.
  • Frequency Cap: To prevent abuse, this option should have a frequency cap, such as once every 15 minutes or a limit of 3 uses per wave.
  • Technical Implementation: Requires integration with the Unity Ads SDK. A state machine will manage the death sequence, offering the ad option and handling the callback to restore health and reset the wave state.

2.1.2. Currency Doubler (US-002)

  • Trigger: Upon successful completion of a wave.
  • Player Action: The player is presented with an option to watch a rewarded video ad.
  • Reward: Upon successful completion of the ad, the currency earned for that specific wave is doubled.
  • Frequency Cap: This can be a per-wave offer with no strict frequency cap, as it is a reward for success.
  • Technical Implementation: Requires integration with the Unity Ads SDK. The wave completion logic must check for ad availability and player choice before awarding currency.

2.2. In-App Purchase (IAP) - Premium Ship (US-003)

  • Product Name: 'Nova' Ship
  • Price: $1.99 USD
  • Reward: Unlocks the 'Nova' ship for the player. This ship will have unique stats (e.g., higher health, different weapon type) and a distinct visual appearance.
  • Unlock Condition: Can be purchased at any time from the Ship Selection screen if the player has sufficient real-world funds.
  • Technical Implementation: Requires integration with the Unity IAP service. A product definition for 'Nova' ship must be created in the Unity Cloud Console. The game must handle the transaction process, validate the purchase with the store, and permanently unlock the ship for the player's account. The player's inventory system must be updated to reflect the new unlock.

3. System Requirements

  • Unity Engine: Version 2022.3 LTS or later.
  • Unity Ads SDK: Version 4.x or later.
  • Unity IAP: Version 4.x or later.
  • Platform Support: iOS, Android.

4. Data Structures

4.1. Player Inventory

This structure will manage all player-owned ships and items.

Field Name Type Description
playerCurrency int The amount of in-game currency the player possesses.
unlockedShips string[] A list of the unique identifiers for all ships unlocked by the player.
equippedShip string The identifier of the ship currently being used by the player.

4.2. Ship Data

This structure defines the properties of each ship. The 'Nova' ship will be added here with its unique stats.

Field Name Type Description
shipID string Unique identifier for the ship (e.g., "Nova").
shipName string The display name of the ship.
baseHealth float The maximum health of the ship.
baseAttack float The base damage the ship deals.
attackSpeed float The time in seconds between attacks.
isPremium bool True if the ship was purchased via IAP, false otherwise.
visualAssetPath string The path to the 3D model and materials for the ship.

4.3. Monetization Configuration

This structure holds the configuration values for the rewarded ad system.

Field Name Type Description
reviveAdID string The specific placement ID for the revive rewarded ad in Unity Ads.
reviveAdCooldownSeconds int The cooldown period in seconds before the revive ad can be used again.
reviveAdHealthReward float The percentage of health restored upon watching the revive ad (e.g., 0.5 for 50%).
currencyDoubleAdID string The specific placement ID for the currency doubling rewarded ad in Unity Ads.

4.4. In-App Purchase Product Definitions

This structure defines the properties of the IAP product.

Field Name Type Description
productID string The unique product identifier for the 'Nova' ship (e.g., "nova_ship_001").
price float The price of the product in USD.
shipIDToUnlock string The shipID of the ship that this IAP unlocks.
shipStatsOverride ShipStats An optional structure to override the default stats of the unlocked ship.

Note: The ShipStatsOverride is a placeholder. The 'Nova' ship's stats will be defined directly in its Ship Data entry and will not be overridden.

Automated ship targeting and combat.

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-001: Player revives after ship death using rewarded ad Given the player's ship has just been destroyed When the player watches a full rewarded video ad Then the player's ship should be instantly respawned at the start of the next wave with 50% health.

US-002: Player doubles currency reward upon completing a wave using rewarded ad Given the player has just successfully completed a wave When the player watches a full rewarded video ad Then the player's currency reward for that wave should be doubled.

US-003: Player purchases a new ship design via IAP Given the player has a valid payment method on file When the player navigates to the 'Ship Customization' menu and confirms the purchase of the 'Stellar Hawk' design for $1.99 Then the 'Stellar Hawk' ship should be permanently unlocked for the player's use.

US-004: Player's ship automatically targets the closest enemy Given the player's ship is actively engaged in combat When a new enemy appears within the ship's targeting range Then the ship's primary weapon should automatically acquire the new enemy as its target.

US-005: Player's ship automatically fires at its current target Given the player's ship has a valid target locked When the player is not actively firing their weapons Then the ship's primary weapon should automatically fire at the locked target at its standard rate of fire.

Technical Specifications

TS-001: Automated Ship Targeting & Combat System

1. Overview

This system governs the player's ship's automated actions in combat, focusing on target acquisition and firing. It is designed to be simple, effective, and a core part of the game's 'set and forget' feel, with player interaction focused on strategic positioning and resource management.

2. Data Structures

2.1 Ship Combat State Component

This component will be attached to the player's ship and will manage its automated combat behavior.

Field Name Type Description
isCombatActive bool Flag indicating if the ship is currently in an active combat state (i.e., within range of enemies).
targetingRange float The maximum distance at which the ship can detect and target enemies.
attackRange float The maximum distance at which the ship can fire its weapons.
attackRateOfFire float The time in seconds between consecutive shots.
timeSinceLastShot float A timer to track when the last shot was fired, used to enforce the attack rate of fire.
currentTarget GameObject A reference to the currently targeted enemy GameObject. Null if no target is selected.
weaponType string The type of weapon the ship is equipped with (e.g., 'Laser', 'Cannon'). Used to determine damage and attack type.
damage float The base damage value of the ship's weapon.
attackType string The type of damage the weapon deals (e.g., 'Kinetic', 'Energy', 'Explosive'). Used for the Combat Effectiveness matrix.
isTargetingEnabled bool Flag to enable or disable automated targeting.
isFiringEnabled bool Flag to enable or disable automated firing.

2.2 Enemy Data (for Targeting)

Each enemy will need data to be targetable.

Field Name Type Description
health float The current health of the enemy.
attackType string The type of damage the enemy deals (e.g., 'Kinetic', 'Energy'). Used for the Combat Effectiveness matrix.
isTargetable bool Flag to determine if the enemy can be targeted by the player's ship.

3. System Logic

3.1 Target Acquisition

  1. If isTargetingEnabled is true and isCombatActive is true, the system will continuously scan for enemies within targetingRange.
  2. The system will prioritize targets based on proximity to the player's ship. The closest valid enemy will be selected as currentTarget.
  3. If the currentTarget is destroyed or moves out of targetingRange, the system will immediately search for a new target.

3.2 Automated Firing

  1. If isFiringEnabled is true and currentTarget is not null, the system will check if the currentTarget is within attackRange.
  2. If the target is in range and timeSinceLastShot has exceeded attackRateOfFire, the weapon will fire.
  3. The weapon will deal damage of attackType to the currentTarget.
  4. The timeSinceLastShot timer will be reset.

3.3 Combat Effectiveness (Rock-Paper-Scissors)

  1. When the player's weapon fires, the system will compare the attackType of the player's weapon against the attackType of the currentTarget.
  2. A simple matrix will determine if the attack is 'Effective', 'Ineffective', or 'Neutral'.
  3. The damage dealt will be modified based on this comparison (e.g., +25% for effective, -25% for ineffective). The matrix will be defined in a separate configuration table (see TS-003).

4. Monetization Integration

4.1 Rewarded Ad - Ship Revival (US-001)

  1. Upon the player's ship being destroyed, a UI prompt will appear offering a revive. This prompt will only appear if the player has not recently used the feature (e.g., a cooldown of 5-10 minutes).
  2. If the player chooses to watch the ad, the Unity Ads SDK will be invoked to play a rewarded video ad.
  3. Upon successful completion of the ad, the player's ship will be instantly respawned at the start of the next wave with 50% health. The isCombatActive flag will be reset, and the game will transition to the next wave. A cooldown timer for this feature will be started.

4.2 Rewarded Ad - Currency Doubling (US-002)

  1. Upon successfully completing a wave, a UI prompt will appear offering to double the currency reward for that wave by watching an ad.
  2. If the player chooses to watch the ad, the Unity Ads SDK will be invoked.
  3. Upon successful completion of the ad, the standard currency reward for the completed wave will be doubled before being added to the player's balance.

4.3 In-App Purchase - New Ship (US-003)

  1. A new ship, the 'Stellar Hawk', will be available for purchase for $1.99.
  2. The player can initiate the purchase from the 'Ship Customization' menu.
  3. The Unity IAP system will handle the transaction with the platform (e.g., Google Play, App Store).
  4. Upon a successful purchase, the 'Stellar Hawk' ship will be permanently unlocked for the player. Its data (stats, appearance) will be added to the player's save file. This provides a one-time purchase for a new, potentially more powerful, ship to encourage financial support and provide value for post-launch updates.

5. System Dependencies

  • Unity Engine
  • Unity Ads SDK
  • Unity IAP SDK
  • Player Save Data Manager
  • Enemy Manager
  • UI Manager

Wave progression with increasing difficulty.

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-001: Wave Completion Doubled Currency

Scenario 1: Player completes a wave and receives double currency. Given the player has 100 currency units. When the player successfully defeats the final enemy of Wave 5. Then the player's currency should be 200 units.

Scenario 2: Player completes a wave and receives standard currency. Given the player has 100 currency units. When the player successfully defeats the final enemy of Wave 1. Then the player's currency should be 110 units.

US-002: Player Revives with 50% Health on Death

Scenario 1: Player chooses to revive after death. Given the player's health is 0% after being defeated in a wave. When the player watches a full rewarded video ad. Then the player's health should be restored to 50% of its maximum value. And the player should remain in the current wave.

Scenario 2: Player chooses not to revive after death. Given the player's health is 0% after being defeated in a wave. When the player chooses not to watch the rewarded video ad. Then the player's health should remain at 0%. And the game should transition to the Game Over screen.

US-003: Player Purchases New Ship Design

Scenario 1: Player successfully purchases a new ship. Given the player has more than $1.99 in currency. When the player navigates to the Ship Customization menu and confirms the purchase of the 'Stardust Cruiser' for $1.99. Then the player's currency should be reduced by $1.99. And the 'Stardust Cruiser' should become available for the player to equip.

Scenario 2: Player attempts to purchase a new ship with insufficient funds. Given the player has less than $1.99 in currency. When the player attempts to purchase the 'Stardust Cruiser' for $1.99. Then a message indicating insufficient funds should be displayed. And the player's currency should remain unchanged.

Technical Specifications

TS-001: Monetization - Rewarded Ads & IAP

1. Overview

This specification details the monetization strategy for 'Solar System Coop', focusing on the integration of Unity Ads for rewarded video and Unity In-App Purchases (IAP) for a premium ship. The goal is to provide value to the player while generating revenue for ongoing development.

2. Rewarded Video Ads (Unity Ads)

2.1. Ad Placement & Reward Logic

Placement ID Trigger Condition Reward Type Reward Value Frequency Capping Notes
AD_REVIVE_DEATH Player's health reaches 0% after being defeated. Health Restore 50% of Max Health 1 per wave (or per 24h) Player must watch a full ad to revive. If not, they proceed to Game Over.
AD_CURRENCY_DOUBLE Player successfully completes a wave. Currency Boost 2x Standard Reward 1 per wave Player has a choice to watch the ad or claim the standard reward.

2.2. Implementation Notes

  • A cooldown or limit must be in place for each ad placement to prevent abuse and maintain player experience.
  • The UI for presenting the ad offer must be clear and non-intrusive.
  • Ad performance and engagement metrics must be tracked to optimize placement and frequency.

3. In-App Purchase (IAP)

3.1. Product Details

Product ID Name Description Price (USD) Currency Cost Stats Bonus Visuals Target Audience
IAP_SHIP_STARDUST Stardust Cruiser A unique, high-performance ship with enhanced shields and a special weapon. $1.99 N/A +20% Shields, +10% Damage, Unique Weapon Unique 3D Model & Effects Players seeking a powerful advantage and unique aesthetic.

3.2. Implementation Notes

  • The IAP product must be configured in the Unity IAP dashboard.
  • The game must handle the full purchase lifecycle: initiating the transaction, handling success, failure, and restoring purchases on app launch.
  • The stats and visual data for the new ship must be stored in a persistent player data file.
  • The UI for the IAP offer must be clear about the one-time cost and the benefits provided.

Technical Specifications

Solar System Coop: Technical Specifications

TS-001: Rewarded Ad Integration - Revive Mechanic

1. Overview

This feature allows players to revive their destroyed ship with 50% health by watching a full Unity Rewarded Video Ad.

2. System Logic

  1. Upon ship destruction, the game pauses and presents a 'Revive?' prompt.
  2. If the player selects 'Revive', the Unity Ads SDK is called to display a rewarded video ad.
  3. Upon successful completion of the ad, the player's ship is instantly respawned at a designated safe location with 50% of its maximum health. The player's currency is not affected.
  4. A cooldown period is applied to prevent immediate re-use of the revive feature (e.g., 5 minutes).

3. Data Structure Impact

No new persistent data is required for this feature, as the state is managed locally by the ad SDK and a short-term cooldown timer.

TS-002: Rewarded Ad Integration - Currency Doubling

1. Overview

This feature allows players to double the currency reward for completing a wave by watching a full Unity Rewarded Video Ad.

2. System Logic

  1. Upon successful completion of a wave, the standard currency reward is calculated.
  2. The game presents a 'Double Reward?' prompt.
  3. If the player selects 'Double Reward', the Unity Ads SDK is called to display a rewarded video ad.
  4. Upon successful completion of the ad, the standard currency reward is doubled before being added to the player's total.
  5. A short cooldown (e.g., 10 minutes) can be applied to prevent excessive spamming.

3. Data Structure Impact

No new persistent data is required, as the logic is applied dynamically at the end of each wave.

TS-003: In-App Purchase (IAP) - New Ship 'Stellar Hawk'

1. Overview

This feature allows players to purchase the 'Stellar Hawk' ship for $1.99 USD, unlocking it permanently for use.

2. System Logic

  1. The 'Stellar Hawk' ship is defined as a premium item in the IAP catalog. Its stats are higher than the starting ship.
  2. The player selects the 'Stellar Hawk' from the ship selection menu.
  3. The game initiates the Unity IAP flow to process the transaction with the specified price.
  4. Upon successful payment confirmation from the store, the 'Stellar Hawk' ship is permanently unlocked for the player. The player's currency is reduced by $1.99.
  5. The purchase is saved locally and can be restored if the game is reinstalled.

3. Data Structure Impact

3.1. Player Data (PlayerState)

Field Name Type Description
currency float The player's in-game currency.
unlockedShips list A list of the unique IDs of all ships unlocked by the player.

3.2. Ship Data (ShipStats)

| Field Name | Type | Description | | shipId | string | Unique identifier for the ship (e.g., 'StellarHawk'). | | name | string | The display name of the ship. | | description | string | A short description of the ship. | | baseHealth | float | The maximum health of the ship. | | baseDamage | float | The base damage output of the ship. | | baseAttackSpeed | float | The time in seconds between attacks. | | isPremium | bool | Flag indicating if the ship was purchased via IAP. | | visualAssetPath | string | The path to the 3D model and prefab for the ship. |

3.3. IAP Product Definition

TS-004: Core Economy & Progression Data

1. Overview

This section defines the data structures for the player's currency, upgrades, and the enemy compendium.

2. System Logic

The player earns currency by defeating enemies and completing waves. This currency is used to purchase upgrades and unlock new ships.

3. Data Structure Impact

3.1. Player Data (PlayerState)

currency float The player's in-game currency.

3.2. Upgrade Data (UpgradeStats)

3.3. Enemy Data (EnemyStats)

| Field Name | Type | Description | | enemyId | string | Unique identifier for the enemy type. | | name | string | The display name of the enemy. | | description | string | A short description of the enemy. | | baseHealth | float | The enemy's maximum health. | | baseDamage | float | The damage the enemy deals. | | attackSpeed | float | The time in seconds between the enemy's attacks. | | movementSpeed | float | The enemy's movement speed. | | weakness | string | The type of damage the enemy is weak against (e.g., 'piercing', 'energy'). | | resistance | string | The type of damage the enemy is resistant to. | | rewardCurrency | int | The amount of currency dropped upon defeat. |

TS-005: Combat Effectiveness (Rock-Paper-Scissors) Logic

1. Overview

This system defines a simple, strategic combat triangle where different damage types are more effective against certain enemy types.

2. System Logic

  1. Each enemy type has a 'weakness' and a 'resistance'.
  2. Each player weapon type has a corresponding 'damage type'.
  3. When a player's weapon damage type matches an enemy's weakness, the damage dealt is multiplied (e.g., by 1.5x).
  4. When a player's weapon damage type matches an enemy's resistance, the damage dealt is reduced (e.g., by 0.5x).

3. Data Structure Impact

3.1. Enemy Data (EnemyStats)

Field Name Type Description
weakness string The type of damage the enemy is weak against (e.g., 'piercing', 'energy').
resistance string The type of damage the enemy is resistant to.

3.2. Weapon Data (WeaponStats)

Field Name Type Description
damageType string The type of damage the weapon deals (e.g., 'kinetic', 'energy', 'piercing').

3.3. Game Configuration

A configuration table or script will be required to define the specific multipliers for each weakness and resistance interaction (e.g., 'piercing_vs_armor = 1.5', 'energy_vs_shields = 0.5').

TS-006: Progression & Upgrade Matrix (Tier 1)

1. Overview

This defines the structure for the first tier of player upgrades, which are unlocked by completing waves.

2. System Logic

Players earn 'upgradePoints' by completing waves. These points can be spent on permanent upgrades that enhance the player's ship or abilities.

3. Data Structure Impact

3.1. Player Data (PlayerState)

3.3. Example Tier 1 Upgrades

Ship and weapon unlocking via progression milestones (Wave 5 for first upgrade).

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-001: Player Revives with Rewind

Scenario 1: Player uses Rewind after death Given the player's ship has just been destroyed When the player taps the 'Revive' button and watches a rewarded ad Then the player's ship should be placed back at the start of the current wave with 50% health.

Scenario 2: Player chooses not to revive Given the player's ship has just been destroyed When the player taps the 'Skip' button or closes the ad Then the game over screen should be displayed.

US-002: Player Doubles Currency on Wave Complete

Scenario 1: Player watches ad to double currency Given the player has just completed a wave and earned 100 currency When the player taps the 'Double Reward' button and watches a rewarded ad Then the player's currency total should increase by 200.

Scenario 2: Player skips the ad to double currency Given the player has just completed a wave and earned 100 currency When the player taps the 'Skip' button to double currency Then the player's currency total should increase by only 100.

Technical Specifications

TS-001: Rewarded Video Ad Integration

1. Overview

This specification details the integration of the Unity Ads SDK to implement a rewarded video ad system for player revival and currency doubling.

2. Ad Placements & Logic

2.1. Ad Placement: Player Revive

  • Trigger: Upon player ship destruction.
  • UI Prompt: A modal appears offering the player a choice: 'Revive (Watch Ad)' or 'Skip'.
  • Rewarded Action: If the player watches the full ad, their ship is reset at the start of the current wave with 50% health. The player is then returned to the main game loop.
  • Skipped Action: If the player taps 'Skip' or closes the ad before completion, the 'Game Over' screen is displayed.

2.2. Ad Placement: Double Currency

  • Trigger: Immediately after a wave is successfully completed.
  • UI Prompt: A modal appears offering the player a choice: 'Double Reward (Watch Ad)' or 'Standard Reward'.
  • Rewarded Action: If the player watches the full ad, their currency reward for that wave is doubled. The player is then returned to the main game loop.
  • Skipped Action: If the player taps 'Skip' or closes the ad, they receive only the standard, non-doubled reward for that wave. The player is then returned to the main game loop.

3. Technical Implementation

3.1. Unity Ads SDK Integration

  • Task: Integrate the official Unity Ads SDK into the project. Configure the ad units for 'Rewarded Video' type.
  • Configuration: Set up two distinct Rewarded Video ad units: one for 'PlayerRevive' and one for 'DoubleCurrency'.

3.2. Ad Manager Service

  • Component: A new global service, AdManager, will be responsible for all ad interactions.
  • Responsibilities:
    • Initializing the Unity Ads SDK.
    • Checking for ad availability (Advertisement.IsReady(adUnitId)).
    • Displaying ads (Advertisement.Show(adUnitId, options)).
    • Handling ad callbacks (success, failure, skipped, closed).
    • Triggering the appropriate game logic based on the ad result.

3.3. State Management Integration

  • The AdManager will communicate with the GameManager and UIManager to:
    • Request the display of the revive/double reward modals.
    • Inform the GameManager when a rewarded ad has been successfully completed to trigger the specific reward logic.
    • Inform the UIManager to show the 'Game Over' screen if the player skips an ad.

4. Monetization Metrics

  • The AdManager will track the number of times each ad unit is shown, watched, and skipped to monitor performance.

Integration of Unity Ads SDK for Rewarded Video Ads.

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-001: Rewarded Video Ad for Player Revival

Scenario 1: Player chooses to revive after death Given the player's health is 0 and they have died When they select the 'Revive with Ad' option Then a rewarded video ad begins playing.

Scenario 2: Player completes the ad and revives Given the player has completed the rewarded video ad When the ad finishes and the 'Revive' button is pressed Then the player's health is restored to 50% And they are placed back at the start of the current wave.

Scenario 3: Player chooses not to revive Given the player's health is 0 and they have died When they select the 'Continue to Menu' option Then they are taken to the main menu.

US-002: Rewarded Video Ad for Wave Completion Bonus

Scenario 1: Player completes a wave and chooses to double currency Given the player has just completed a wave When they select the 'Double Currency with Ad' option Then a rewarded video ad begins playing.

Scenario 2: Player completes the ad and receives the bonus Given the player has completed the rewarded video ad When the ad finishes and the 'Claim Bonus' button is pressed Then the currency earned for that wave is doubled.

US-003: In-App Purchase for New Ship Design

Scenario 1: Player purchases the new ship Given the player is on the Ship Select screen When they purchase the 'Stellar Cruiser' for $1.99 Then the 'Stellar Cruiser' is added to their owned ships.

Scenario 2: Player equips the new ship Given the player owns the 'Stellar Cruiser' When they select and equip it Then the 'Stellar Cruiser' is now the active ship in the game.

Overview\nThis specification details the integration of the Unity Ads SDK to implement rewarded video ad functionality for player revival and currency doubling. This is a core part of the monetization strategy for 'Solar System Coop'.\n\n## 2. Data Structures\n\n### 2.1. Ad Placement Configuration\nThis configuration will store the specific placement IDs for each rewarded ad type.\n\n| Field Name | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| reviveAdPlacementId | String | The unique placement ID for the rewarded ad shown upon player death. |\n| doubleCurrencyAdPlacementId | String | The unique placement ID for the rewarded ad shown at wave completion. |\n\n### 2.2. Ad State Variables\nThese variables will track the player's ability to watch ads.\n\n| Field Name | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| canWatchReviveAd | Boolean | Flag indicating if the player is eligible to watch the revive ad (e.g., not on cooldown). Defaults to true. |\n| canWatchDoubleCurrencyAd | Boolean | Flag indicating if the player is eligible to watch the double currency ad (e.g., not on cooldown). Defaults to true. |\n| lastReviveAdWatchTime | Timestamp | The date and time the last revive ad was watched. Used for cooldown calculation. |\n| lastDoubleCurrencyAdWatchTime | Timestamp | The date and time the last double currency ad was watched. Used for cooldown calculation. |\n\n## 3. System Logic\n\n### 3.1. Player Revival Ad Flow\n1. On Player Death: The game checks the canWatchReviveAd flag. If true, the 'Revive with Ad' option is displayed.\n2. User Selects Ad: The game calls the Unity Ads SDK to show the reviveAdPlacementId ad.\n3. Ad Completion: Upon successful ad completion, the game sets canWatchReviveAd to false and records the current time in lastReviveAdWatchTime.\n4. Revive Action: The game restores the player's health to 50% and places them back at the start of the current wave.\n5. Cooldown: A timer is started to re-enable canWatchReviveAd after a specified duration (e.g., 30 minutes).\n\n### 3.2. Double Currency Ad Flow\n1. On Wave Complete: The game checks the canWatchDoubleCurrencyAd flag. If true, the 'Double Currency with Ad' option is displayed.\n2. User Selects Ad: The game calls the Unity Ads SDK to show the doubleCurrencyAdPlacementId ad.\n3. Ad Completion: Upon successful ad completion, the game sets canWatchDoubleCurrencyAd to false and records the current time in lastDoubleCurrencyAdWatchTime.\n4. Bonus Action: The currency earned for the completed wave is doubled and added to the player's balance.\n5. Cooldown: A timer is started to re-enable canWatchDoubleCurrencyAd after a specified duration (e.g., 1 hour).\n\n## 4. Technical Implementation Notes\n* A MonetizationManager script will be responsible for handling all ad interactions and state management.\n* The ad cooldowns must be persistent across game sessions. This will require saving the lastAdWatchTime values to player preferences.\n* Error handling for ad loading failures, ad display failures, and user interruptions is crucial.\n\n# TS-002: In-App Purchase (IAP) for New Ship\n\n## 1. Overview\nThis specification details the implementation of a single In-App Purchase (IAP) for a new, premium ship called the 'Stellar Cruiser'. This provides a direct revenue stream and enhances the player's options.\n\n## 2. Data Structures\n\n### 2.1. Product Configuration\nThis configuration will store the details of the IAP product.\n\n| Field Name | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| stellarCruiserProductId | String | The unique product ID for the 'Stellar Cruiser' in the store (e.g., "com.yourcompany.solarsystemcoop.stellarcruiser"). |\n| stellarCruiserPrice | Float | The price of the product in USD. Set to 1.99. |\n| stellarCruiserCurrency | String | The currency of the price (e.g., "USD"). |\n\n### 2.2. Player Inventory\nThe player's owned ships are managed in the PlayerInventory data structure.\n\n| Field Name | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| ownedShips | Array of Strings | A list of the unique IDs of all ships owned by the player. Initially contains only the default ship ID. |\n\n### 2.3. Ship Data\nThe ShipData table will be expanded to include the new ship.\n\n| Field Name | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| shipId | String | Unique identifier for the ship (e.g., "stellar_cruiser"). |\n| shipName | String | The display name of the ship (e.g., "Stellar Cruiser"). |\n| shipDescription | String | A short description of the ship's lore or purpose. |\n| shipStats | Object | A container for the ship's gameplay stats. |\n| shipStats.health | Float | The base health of the ship. (e.g., 150) |\n| shipStats.attackPower | Float | The base damage the ship deals. (e.g., 25) |\n| shipStats.attackSpeed | Float | The time between attacks. (e.g., 1.2s) |\n| shipStats.movementSpeed | Float | The ship's base movement speed. (e.g., 1.0) |\n| isPremium | Boolean | Flag indicating if this ship is a paid unlock. Set to true for the Stellar Cruiser. |\n\n## 3. System Logic\n\n### 3.1. Purchasing the Ship\n1. On Ship Select Screen: The 'Stellar Cruiser' is displayed with its price and a 'Purchase' button.\n2. User Selects Purchase: The game initiates the Unity IAP flow for the stellarCruiserProductId.\n3. Purchase Success: Upon a successful transaction, the stellarCruiserProductId is added to the ownedShips array in the player's inventory. The isPremium flag for the 'Stellar Cruiser' in the ShipData table is set to true. The player is then taken back to the Ship Select screen, and the 'Stellar Cruiser' is now available to be equipped.\n4. Purchase Failure/Cancellation: The player is returned to the Ship Select screen with no changes to their inventory.\n\n### 3.2. Equipping the Ship\n1. On Ship Select Screen: The 'Stellar Cruiser' is now selectable and marked as owned.\n2. User Selects Ship: The player taps on the 'Stellar Cruiser' to equip it.\n3. Update Game State: The game updates its internal state to use the shipId and stats of the 'Stellar Cruiser' for the current game session.\n\n## 4. Technical Implementation Notes\n* The PlayerInventoryManager will be responsible for managing the ownedShips list and interacting with the IAP system.\n* The ShipData table will be loaded from a configuration file (e.g., JSON, Scriptable Objects) and updated at runtime if a new ship is purchased.\n* Robust error handling for IAP transactions (e.g., network errors, store errors) is required.\n* The isPremium flag is essential for differentiating between free and paid ships in the UI and logic.\n\n# TS-003: Combat Effectiveness (Rock-Paper-Scissors) System\n\n## 1. Overview\nThis specification details the implementation of the Combat Effectiveness (RPS) system, a core strategic element of the game. This system creates a dynamic rock-paper-scissors relationship between different ship types and enemy types.\n\n## 2. Data Structures\n\n### 2.1. Ship Type Enum\nAn enum to define the different combat roles of ships.\n\n| Value | Description |\n|---|---|\n| Standard | A balanced, general-purpose ship type. |\n| Aggressive | A ship focused on high damage output. |\n| Defensive | A ship focused on high health and damage mitigation. |\n\n### 2.2. Enemy Type Enum\nAn enum to define the different combat roles of enemies.\n\n| Value | Description |\n|---|---|\n| Standard | A balanced, general-purpose enemy type. |\n| Fast | An enemy focused on high speed and evasion. |\n| Heavy | An enemy focused on high health and armor. |\n\n### 2.3. Effectiveness Matrix\nA table defining the damage multiplier for each ship type attacking each enemy type.\n\n| Attacker \ Defender | Standard Enemy | Fast Enemy | Heavy Enemy |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Standard Ship | 1.0x | 1.0x | 1.0x |\n| Aggressive Ship | 1.0x | 1.5x | 0.5x |\n| Defensive Ship | 1.0x | 0.5x | 1.5x |\n\n### 2.4. Ship Data Extension\nThe ShipData table must include the ship's combat type.\n\n| Field Name | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| shipId | String | Unique identifier for the ship. |\n| shipName | String | The display name of the ship. |\n| shipDescription | String | A short description of the ship. |\n| shipStats | Object | A container for the ship's gameplay stats. |\n| shipStats.health | Float | The base health of the ship. |\n| shipStats.attackPower | Float | The base damage the ship deals. |\n| shipStats.attackSpeed | Float | The time between attacks. |\n| shipStats.movementSpeed | Float | The ship's base movement speed. |\n| shipStats.combatType | String | The combat type of the ship (e.g., "Standard", "Aggressive", "Defensive"). |\n\n### 2.5. Enemy Data Extension\nThe EnemyData table must include the enemy's combat type.\n\n| Field Name | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| enemyId | String | Unique identifier for the enemy. |\n| enemyName | String | The display name of the enemy. |\n| enemyDescription | String | A short description of the enemy. |\n| enemyStats | Object | A container for the enemy's gameplay stats. |\n| enemyStats.health | Float | The base health of the enemy. |\n| enemyStats.attackPower | Float | The damage the enemy deals. |\n| enemyStats.attackSpeed | Float | The time between attacks. |\n| enemyStats.movementSpeed | Float | The enemy's base movement speed. |\n| enemyStats.combatType | String | The combat type of the enemy (e.g., "Standard", "Fast", "Heavy"). |\n\n## 3. System Logic\n\n### 3.1. Calculating Damage\nWhen a ship attacks an enemy:\n1. The game retrieves the combatType of the attacking ship and the target enemy.\n2. It looks up the corresponding damage multiplier in the Effectiveness Matrix.\n3. The final damage dealt is calculated as: (Attacking Ship's Attack Power) * (Damage Multiplier).\n\n### 3.2. Strategic Implications\n* Players must choose their ship based on the types of enemies they are facing. For example, a Defensive ship is ideal against Heavy enemies.\n* The system encourages players to experiment with different ship and enemy type combinations to find optimal strategies.\n\n## 4. Technical Implementation Notes\n* The CombatManager will be responsible for performing the damage calculation using the matrix.\n* The ShipData and EnemyData tables must be designed to easily accommodate the new combatType field.\n\n# TS-004: Progression & Upgrade System\n\n## 1. Overview\nThis specification details the initial progression and upgrade system for 'Solar System Coop', focusing on unlocking new ships and enhancing existing ones through a structured milestone system.\n\n## 2. Data Structures\n\n### 2.1. Ship Data (Extended)\nThe ShipData table will be expanded to include upgrade information.\n\n| Field Name | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| shipId | String | Unique identifier for the ship. |\n| shipName | String | The display name of the ship. |\n| shipDescription | String | A short description of the ship. |\n| shipStats | Object | A container for the ship's gameplay stats. |\n| shipStats.health | Float | The base health of the ship. |\n| shipStats.attackPower | Float | The base damage the ship deals. |\n| shipStats.attackSpeed | Float | The time between attacks. |\n| shipStats.movementSpeed | Float | The ship's base movement speed. |\n| shipStats.combatType | String | The combat type of the ship. |\n| isPremium | Boolean | Flag indicating if this ship is a paid unlock. |\n| unlockWave | Integer | The wave number at which this ship becomes available for purchase. Defaults to 0 for the starting ship. |\n| upgradePath | String | The shipId of the next ship in its upgrade path, or null if it's the final ship. |\n\n### 2.3. Player Progression Data\nThis data will be saved per player.\n\n| Field Name | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| currentWave | Integer | The highest wave the player has reached. Defaults to 1. |\n| currency | Integer | The player's in-game currency. Defaults to 100. |\n| ownedShips | Array of Strings | A list of the unique IDs of all ships owned by the player. (e.g., ["basic_fighter", "stellar_cruiser"]) |\n| equippedShipId | String | The shipId of the currently active ship. Defaults to "basic_fighter". |\n\n## 3. System Logic\n\n### 3.1. Unlocking New Ships\n* At the start of each new wave, the game checks if the currentWave has met or exceeded the unlockWave for any unowned ships.\n* If a ship's unlockWave is met, it is added to the player's ownedShips list. The isPremium flag is set based on its configuration.\n* The unlockWave for that ship is then set to a value higher than the current wave to prevent it from being unlocked again.\n\n### 3.2. Upgrading Ships\n* The upgradePath field in ShipData defines the progression. For example, the basic_fighter might have an upgradePath of "advanced_fighter".\n* When a player wants to upgrade, they must own the current ship and have enough currency. The cost of the upgrade is defined by the target ship's data (e.g., its unlockWave value could be used as a proxy for cost, or a separate cost field could be added).\n* Upon a successful upgrade purchase, the player's currency is deducted, and their ownedShips list is updated to replace the old ship with the new one. The equippedShipId is also updated.\n\n### 3.3. Progression Milestones\n* Wave 1: Player starts with the basic_fighter. currency = 100. ownedShips = ["basic_fighter"].\n* Wave 5: The advanced_fighter is unlocked and added to ownedShips. Its unlockWave is updated.\n* Wave 10: The heavy_destroyer is unlocked and added to ownedShips. Its unlockWave is updated.\n\n## 4. Technical Implementation Notes\n* Player progression data must be saved and loaded reliably (e.g., using PlayerPrefs or a save file system).\n* The ShipData table will need to be managed carefully to ensure unlockWave values are updated correctly after a ship is unlocked.\n* The upgrade system should be designed to be extensible for future ships and upgrades.\n\n# TS-005: Enemy Compendium Data Structure\n\n## 1. Overview\nThis specification defines the data structure for enemy types, allowing for a variety of challenges in the game.\n\n## 2. Data Structures\n\n### 2.1. Defaults to 1. |\n\n## 3. Example Enemy Data\n\n### 3.1. Rewarded Ad placement upon ship death for a 50% health revive.

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-001 Scenario 1: Player chooses to revive after ship death Given the player's ship has been destroyed When the 'Revive' button with the rewarded ad icon is displayed And the player taps the 'Revive' button Then the Unity Ads SDK should initiate the display of a rewarded video ad.

US-002 Scenario 2: Player successfully completes the rewarded ad to revive Given the player has initiated the revive process and the ad is playing When the rewarded video ad finishes playing completely And the player taps the 'Continue' button to return to the game Then the player's ship should be respawned with 50% of its maximum health.

US-003 Scenario 3: Player chooses not to revive after ship death Given the player's ship has been destroyed When the 'Revive' button with the rewarded ad icon is displayed And the player taps the 'Skip' or 'No Thanks' button Then the game should proceed to the 'Game Over' screen.

US-004 Scenario 4: Player has already used the revive in the current session Given the player has already used the rewarded ad revive once in the current session When their ship is destroyed again Then the 'Revive' button with the rewarded ad icon should not be displayed, and only the 'Game Over' option should be available.

Technical Specifications

TS-001: Rewarded Ad - Revive System

1. Overview

This feature allows the player to revive their ship with 50% health after destruction by watching a rewarded video ad. This is intended as a primary monetization and player retention tool.

2. Data Structure

Field Name Data Type Description Required Notes
maxRevivesPerSession integer The maximum number of times the player can use the revive feature per session. Yes Set to 1 for MVP.
currentRevivesUsed integer The number of times the player has used the revive feature in the current session. Yes Resets to 0 when the game is closed and reopened.
reviveAdRewardHealth float The percentage of maximum health granted upon watching the ad. Yes Set to 0.5 (50%).

3. System Logic

  1. When the player's ship is destroyed, the game checks currentRevivesUsed. If it is less than maxRevivesPerSession, the 'Revive' button with the ad icon is displayed. Otherwise, only the 'Game Over' option is shown.
  2. If the player taps 'Revive', the Unity Ads SDK is called to play a rewarded video ad.
  3. Upon successful completion of the ad, the player's ship is respawned with health set to maxHealth * reviveAdRewardHealth. currentRevivesUsed is incremented.
  4. If the player skips the ad or closes it before completion, the game proceeds to the 'Game Over' screen, and currentRevivesUsed remains unchanged.

TS-002: Rewarded Ad - Currency Doubler

1. Overview

This feature allows the player to double the amount of currency earned upon completing a wave by watching a rewarded video ad.

2. Data Structure

Field Name Data Type Description Required Notes
currencyDoublerAdID string The specific placement ID for the wave completion rewarded ad in the Unity Ads dashboard. Yes A unique identifier for this ad placement.

3. System Logic

  1. Upon successfully completing a wave, the 'Wave Complete' screen is shown, displaying the base currency reward.
  2. A 'Double Reward' button with the ad icon is displayed.
  3. If the player taps the button, the Unity Ads SDK is called to play a rewarded video ad.
  4. Upon successful completion of the ad, the player receives double the base currency reward. If the player skips or closes the ad, they only receive the base reward.

TS-003: In-App Purchase - New Ship

1. Overview

This feature allows players to purchase a new, unique ship for a one-time fee of $1.99. This ship will have its own stats and visual representation.

2. Data Structure

2.1. Product Definition (for Unity IAP)

Field Name Data Type Description Required Notes
productId string The unique identifier for the product in the store. Yes e.g., "com.devdoctorai.solarsystemcoop.ship_phoenix"
type string The type of product. Yes Set to "consumable" or "nonconsumable". For a ship, it should be nonconsumable.
price float The price of the product in USD. Yes Set to 1.99.
currency string The currency code for the price. Yes e.g., "USD".

2.2. Player Inventory Data

Field Name Data Type Description Required Notes
ownedShips array of strings A list of the product IDs of all ships owned by the player. Yes Starts with the default ship's ID. e.g., ["com.devdoctorai.solarsystemcoop.ship_default"]

3. System Logic

  1. The 'Shop' screen will display the new ship for purchase at $1.99.
  2. When the player taps 'Purchase', the Unity IAP system is invoked to process the transaction.
  3. Upon successful payment, the productId of the new ship is added to the ownedShips array in the player's persistent data.
  4. The player's ship selection screen will now show the new ship as an available option to equip.

TS-004: Ship Data Structure (Updated)

1. Overview

This document defines the data structure for all player ships, including the new premium ship. It expands on the initial design to include stats relevant to the Combat Effectiveness matrix.

2. Data Tables

2.1. Ship Stats Table

Field Name Data Type Description Required Notes

4. System Logic

  2. The Ship Progression Data table will define the upgrade path for each ship. The player can spend currency to increase their stats.
  3. The ownedShips array in player inventory will determine which ships are available to select and upgrade.

Rewarded Ad placement at Wave Complete to double currency earned.

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-001 Scenario 1: Player successfully doubles currency by watching a rewarded ad after completing a wave Given the player has just completed a wave and earned 100 currency When the player chooses to watch a rewarded ad Then the player should be shown a full-screen video ad And upon the ad's completion, the player's currency should be increased to 200.

Technical Specifications

TS-001: Rewarded Ad Integration - Wave Complete Bonus

1. Overview

This specification details the technical implementation for the 'Wave Complete' rewarded ad feature. The goal is to provide players with an optional incentive to watch a full-screen video ad upon successfully completing a wave, thereby doubling their earned currency.

2. System Architecture

The system will be integrated into the Wave Manager and Economy Manager. The Wave Manager will notify the Economy Manager upon successful wave completion, triggering the ad prompt.

3. Data Structures

No new persistent data structures are required for this specific feature, as it relies on the existing Economy Manager to handle currency transactions.

4. Implementation Steps

  1. Modify Wave Manager: Upon a successful wave completion, before awarding standard currency, the Wave Manager will call a new function on the Economy Manager to check if an ad should be offered.
  2. Call Ad SDK: The Economy Manager will initiate a request to the Unity Ads SDK for a rewarded video ad.
  3. Handle Ad Callback: Implement callbacks for the ad's lifecycle (OnAdStarted, OnAdCompleted, OnAdFailed, OnAdClosed).
  4. Process Reward: Upon a successful OnAdCompleted callback, the Economy Manager will calculate the bonus currency (standard reward * 2) and add it to the player's balance.
  5. Implement Cooldown/Rate Limiting: To prevent abuse, a simple cooldown or a limit on how many times this bonus can be claimed per session or per day should be implemented. This will be managed by a new variable in the Player Data structure.

5. Technical Dependencies

  • Unity Engine
  • Unity Ads SDK (v4.0 or later)

6. Success Metrics

  • Ad Impression Rate: The percentage of completed waves where the player chose to watch an ad.
  • Player Retention: An increase in player retention for sessions where the feature is used.

Integration of Unity IAP for a single $1.99 premium ship with unique stats and visuals.

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-001 Scenario 1: Player purchases the new ship Given the player is on the main menu and has sufficient funds (e.g., $1.99) When the player navigates to the ship selection screen and taps the 'Purchase' button for the new premium ship Then the Unity IAP system should initiate a purchase flow, and upon successful completion, the player should own the new ship and it should be available for selection.

US-002 Scenario 2: Player uses the new ship in a match Given the player has successfully purchased the new ship When they select and start a match with the new ship Then the game should load with the new ship's unique visuals and stats active.

US-003 Scenario 3: Player fails a match and chooses to revive Given the player is in a match and their ship's health reaches zero When the 'Ship Destroyed' screen appears and they tap the 'Revive' button Then the Unity Ads SDK should display a rewarded video ad, and upon completion, the player's ship should be restored to 50% health and the match should resume.

US-004 Scenario 4: Player completes a wave and chooses to double currency Given the player has successfully completed a wave in a match When the 'Wave Complete' screen appears and they tap the 'Double Reward' button Then the Unity Ads SDK should display a rewarded video ad, and upon completion, the player's currency reward for that wave should be doubled.

US-005 Scenario 5: Player attempts to purchase a ship they already own Given the player has already purchased the new premium ship When they navigate to the ship selection screen and tap the 'Purchase' button for the same ship again Then the IAP system should recognize ownership and either disable the purchase button or inform the player they already own the item, without charging them again.

Technical Specifications

Solar System Coop: Technical Specifications

1. System Architecture Overview

The game will be developed using the Unity engine. The architecture will be designed with a modular approach to support future expansion, particularly for co-op multiplayer. The core systems will manage game state, player progression, and monetization.

2. Core Systems Specifications

TS-001: Game State Manager

This system is responsible for managing the overall state of the game (e.g., Main Menu, In-Game, Wave Complete, Ship Destroyed).

Field Name Type Description
currentState enum The current state of the game. Possible values: MainMenu, InGame, WaveComplete, ShipDestroyed.
previousState enum Stores the state prior to entering ShipDestroyed to allow returning to the match.
isPaused bool Flag to indicate if the game is paused.

TS-002: Player Progression Manager

This system handles all player unlocks and progression.

Field Name Type Description
playerCurrency int The amount of in-game currency the player possesses.
unlockedShips List A list of the unique identifiers for all ships the player has unlocked.
ownedShip_Premium bool A flag indicating if the player has purchased the single $1.99 premium ship.

TS-003: Economy Manager

Manages all currency transactions and rewards.

Field Name Type Description
baseWaveReward int The standard amount of currency awarded for completing a wave.
doubleRewardMultiplier int The multiplier applied when a rewarded ad is watched at Wave Complete. Set to 2.

TS-004: Ad Manager (Unity Ads)

This system interfaces with the Unity Ads SDK to display rewarded video ads.

Field Name Type Description
adUnitId_Revive string The specific ad unit ID for the Ship Death revive ad.
adUnitId_DoubleReward string The specific ad unit ID for the Wave Complete double reward ad.
isReviveAdReady bool Flag to track if a revive ad is available to be shown.
isDoubleRewardAdReady bool Flag to track if a double reward ad is available to be shown.

TS-005: IAP Manager (Unity IAP)

This system interfaces with the Unity IAP SDK to handle the premium ship purchase.

Field Name Type Description
premiumShipProduct_ID string The unique product ID for the $1.99 premium ship in the store.
isPremiumShipOwned bool A flag that is set to true upon successful purchase and loaded from player data.

3. Data Structures

TS-006: Ship Data Structure

Defines the properties of each ship in the game.

Field Name Type Description
shipId string A unique identifier for the ship (e.g., "ship_basic", "ship_premium_01").
shipName string The display name of the ship.
stats ShipStats A nested object containing the ship's core statistics.
visualAssetPath string The path to the ship's 3D model and materials.
isPremium bool Flag indicating if this ship is a paid item.

TS-007: Ship Stats Structure

Contains the core combat and performance attributes of a ship.

Field Name Type Description
maxHealth float The total health of the ship.
currentHealth float The current health of the ship.
attackDamage float The base damage dealt by the ship's weapons.
attackSpeed float The time between attacks.
movementSpeed float The ship's base movement speed.
armorType enum The type of damage the ship is resistant to (e.g., Kinetic, Energy, Explosive).

TS-008: Enemy Data Structure

Defines the properties of each enemy type.

Field Name Type Description
enemyId string A unique identifier for the enemy type.
enemyName string The display name of the enemy.
stats EnemyStats A nested object containing the enemy's core attributes.
armorType enum The type of damage the enemy is weak to.
visualAssetPath string The path to the enemy's 3D model and materials.

TS-009: Enemy Stats Structure

Contains the core attributes of an enemy.

Field Name Type Description
maxHealth float The total health of the enemy.
currentHealth float The current health of the enemy.
attackDamage float The damage the enemy deals.
attackSpeed float The time between enemy attacks.
movementSpeed float The enemy's base movement speed.

4. Monetization Flow & Logic

TS-010: Premium Ship Purchase Flow

  1. Trigger: Player taps 'Purchase' on the premium ship in the Ship Selection screen.
  2. Validation: The IAPManager checks the isPremiumShipOwned flag. If true, it informs the player and returns.
  3. Initiate Purchase: If not owned, the IAPManager calls the Unity IAP system to start the transaction for premiumShipProduct_ID.
  4. Success Callback: Upon successful payment confirmation from the store, the IAPManager sets isPremiumShipOwned to true, adds the ship to the player's unlockedShips list, and saves this data.
  5. Reward: The player is returned to the Ship Selection screen, and the premium ship is now available to purchase or equip.

TS-011: Revive Rewarded Ad Flow

  1. Trigger: Player's ship health reaches zero in-game.
  2. Display Prompt: The 'Ship Destroyed' screen appears with a 'Revive' button and a countdown timer. A UI element indicates the reward (e.g., 'Watch Ad to Revive').
  3. Ad Request: The player taps 'Revive'. The AdManager checks if isReviveAdReady is true and requests a rewarded video ad.
  4. Ad Display: If an ad is available, it is displayed to the player.
  5. Ad Completion: Upon successful ad completion, the AdManager receives a callback.
  6. Reward: The PlayerProgressionManager sets the player's ship health to 50% of maxHealth, sets isReviveAdReady to false (with a cooldown), and signals the GameStateManager to resume the match.
  7. Ad Failure/Close: If the ad fails to load or is closed early, the player is returned to the 'Ship Destroyed' screen, and the option to revive may be disabled or the cooldown applied.

TS-012: Double Reward Rewarded Ad Flow

  1. Trigger: Player completes a wave.
  2. Display Prompt: The 'Wave Complete' screen appears with a 'Double Reward' button and a countdown timer. A UI element indicates the reward (e.g., 'Watch Ad to Double Currency').
  3. Ad Request: The player taps 'Double Reward'. The AdManager checks if isDoubleRewardAdReady is true and requests a rewarded video ad.
  4. Ad Display: If an ad is available, it is displayed to the player.
  5. Ad Completion: Upon successful ad completion, the AdManager receives a callback.
  6. Reward: The EconomyManager calculates the standard reward, doubles it, and adds it to the player's playerCurrency. It then sets isDoubleRewardAdReady to false (with a cooldown).
  7. Ad Failure/Close: If the ad fails to load or is closed early, the player receives only the standard reward, and the option to double may be disabled or the cooldown applied.

5. Future Considerations

  • Ad Cooldowns: Implement robust cooldown timers for rewarded ads to prevent abuse and maintain player experience.
  • Ad Placement Tuning: Monitor ad placement frequency and player engagement to optimize the placement and frequency of ad prompts.
  • Progression Balancing: Adjust the currency rewards and unlock requirements based on player data and feedback.
  • Multiplayer State: Design the data structures and network communication protocols for future co-op features.
  • Error Handling: Implement comprehensive error handling for ad and IAP operations.

Implementation of the Combat Effectiveness (Rock-Paper-Scissors) matrix.

▼

User Stories & Criteria

Solar System Coop - Combat Effectiveness (Rock-Paper-Scissors)

US-001: Player successfully rewinds time

Given the player has 3 'Rewind' charges available When they activate the 'Rewind' ability on their ship Then their ship should be instantly moved back to its position 5 seconds prior, and their charge count should decrease to 2.

US-002: Player successfully revives after death with rewarded ad

Given the player's ship has been destroyed When they choose to 'Revive' and watch a full rewarded ad video Then their ship should respawn at the start of the current wave with 50% health, and the ad should be marked as completed for future use.

US-003: Player successfully doubles currency with rewarded ad

Given the player has just completed a wave When they choose to watch a full rewarded ad video Then they should receive double the standard currency reward for that wave.

US-004: Player purchases new ship design

Given the player has sufficient real-money funds When they navigate to the IAP menu and confirm the purchase of the 'Stellar Hawk' ship for $1.99 Then the 'Stellar Hawk' should be permanently unlocked and available for selection in the hangar.

Technical Specifications

TS-001: Combat Effectiveness (Rock-Paper-Scissors) Matrix

1. Overview

This document defines the data structure and logic for the Combat Effectiveness system, which creates a strategic advantage based on a Rock-Paper-Scissors relationship between different ship types.

2. Data Structure

2.1. Ship Type Enum

An enum to define the different combat roles.

Field Name Type Description
shipType String The unique identifier for the ship's combat role (e.g., "Fighter", "Interceptor", "Bomber").

2.2. Effectiveness Matrix

A table that defines the advantage of one ship type over another.

Attacker Type Defender Type Advantage (1=Advantage, 0=Neutral, -1=Disadvantage)
Fighter Interceptor 1
Fighter Bomber -1
Interceptor Bomber 1
Interceptor Fighter -1
Bomber Fighter 1
Bomber Interceptor -1

3. Logic

When a ship attacks another, its damage output will be modified based on the relationship defined in the Effectiveness Matrix. For example, a Fighter attacking an Interceptor will deal 1.5x its base damage (assuming a 0.5 multiplier for disadvantage).

4. Implementation Notes

This matrix will be a data asset (e.g., a Scriptable Object in Unity) that the combat system references to calculate damage. The ship types themselves will be defined in the ShipData structure.

User Stories & Criteria

US-001 Scenario 1: Player revives after ship death using a rewarded ad Given the player's ship has been destroyed When they choose to watch a rewarded ad Then their ship should be instantly revived with 50% health, and the ad should be marked as watched for this session.

US-002 Scenario 2: Player doubles currency after completing a wave using a rewarded ad Given the player has just completed a wave When they choose to watch a rewarded ad Then they should receive double the standard wave completion currency reward, and the ad should be marked as watched for this session.

User Stories & Criteria

US-001: Rewind on Ship Death

Scenario 1: Player revives after ship death Given the player's ship has 0 health and is destroyed When the player watches a full rewarded ad Then the player's ship should be instantly revived with 50% health And the player should not lose any of their currently held currency.

Scenario 2: Player chooses not to revive after ship death Given the player's ship has 0 health and is destroyed When the player chooses not to watch the rewarded ad Then the game should transition to the 'Game Over' screen.

US-002: Double Currency on Wave Complete

Scenario 1: Player completes a wave without using a boost Given the player has 100 currency When the player successfully completes a wave Then the player should be awarded 200 currency.

Scenario 2: Player completes a wave after using a boost Given the player has 100 currency And the player used a 'Double Currency' boost during the wave When the player successfully completes the wave Then the player should be awarded 400 currency.

US-003: Purchase New Ship Design

Scenario 1: Player purchases a new ship design Given the player has $1.99 in their account When the player confirms the purchase of the 'Stellar Hawk' ship for $1.99 Then the player's account should be debited $1.99 And the 'Stellar Hawk' ship should become available for selection in the hangar.

Scenario 2: Player attempts to purchase with insufficient funds Given the player has $0.50 in their account When the player attempts to purchase the 'Stellar Hawk' ship for $1.99 Then the purchase should fail And an 'Insufficient Funds' error message should be displayed.

Technical Specifications

TS-001: Rewarded Video Ads Integration

1. Overview

This specification details the integration of the Unity Ads SDK to implement two key rewarded video ad features: a 'Revive on Death' option and a 'Double Currency on Wave Complete' bonus. This monetization strategy aims to provide value to the player while generating revenue.

2. Rewive on Death (US-001)

2.1. Trigger Condition

This ad option will be presented to the player immediately after their ship's health reaches zero and is destroyed.

2.2. Player Choice

A pop-up UI will appear offering the player two choices: 'Revive (Watch Ad)' or 'Game Over'.

2.3. Ad Display

If the player selects 'Revive', a full-screen rewarded video ad from Unity Ads will be played. The ad must be skippable after a minimum of 15 seconds.

2.4. Post-Ad Logic

Upon successful completion of the ad (or after the minimum skip time has passed), the player's ship will be instantly revived with 50% of its maximum health. The player's current currency total will remain unchanged.

2.5. Failure Logic

If the player closes the ad before completion or selects 'Game Over', the game will transition to the 'Game Over' screen as normal.

3. Double Currency on Wave Complete (US-002)

3.1. Trigger Condition

This ad option will be presented to the player immediately after they successfully complete a wave.

3.2. Player Choice

A pop-up UI will appear offering the player a choice: 'Collect Standard Reward' or 'Double Reward (Watch Ad)'.

3.3. Ad Display

If the player selects 'Double Reward', a full-screen rewarded video ad from Unity Ads will be played. The ad must be skippable after a minimum of 15 seconds.

3.4. Post-Ad Logic

Upon successful completion of the ad, the player's currency reward for that wave will be doubled. For example, a standard 200 currency reward will become 400. The player's current currency total will be updated accordingly.

3.5. Failure Logic

If the player closes the ad or selects 'Collect Standard Reward', they will only receive the standard, non-doubled currency reward for that wave.

4. System Requirements

4.1. SDK Integration

Requires the latest stable version of the Unity Ads SDK to be imported and configured within the Unity project.

4.2. Ad Placement IDs

Specific placement IDs for the 'Revive' and 'Double Currency' rewarded ad types must be obtained from the Unity Ads dashboard and configured in the game's settings.

4.3. State Management

The game's state manager must be updated to handle the new ad-related states (Ad Pending, Ad Rewarded, Ad Failed, Ad Skipped) and to correctly apply the consequences of each choice.

Core state management for Combat, Upgrade, and Monetization states.
