User Stories & Criteria

US-001 Scenario 1: Player revives after ship death using a rewarded ad Given the player's ship has been destroyed When the player chooses to watch a rewarded ad on the 'Game Over' screen Then the player's ship should be instantly revived with 50% health, and the 'Game Over' screen should be dismissed.

US-002 Scenario 2: Player doubles currency after completing a wave using a rewarded ad Given the player has just completed a wave of enemies When the player chooses to watch a rewarded ad on the 'Wave Complete' screen Then the player's currency reward for that wave should be doubled.

US-003 Scenario 3: Player purchases the new ship design Given the player is on the main menu or in the shop When the player selects the new ship design and confirms the purchase for $1.99 Then the $1.99 payment should be processed successfully via the Unity IAP system. And the new ship design should become permanently unlocked and available for the player to select in the hangar.

US-004 Scenario 4: Player attempts to purchase the new ship design with insufficient funds Given the player has insufficient funds in their account to purchase the new ship design When the player attempts to purchase the new ship design for $1.99 Then the purchase should fail. And an appropriate error message should be displayed to the player.

Technical Specifications

TS-001: Core State Management & Game Flow

1. Overview

This specification defines the high-level state machine and core data structures for managing the game's progression, combat, upgrades, and monetization. It serves as the central hub for all game logic.

2. Data Structures

2.1 GameState Manager

Manages the overall game's current state and player progress.

Field Name Type Description
currentWave integer The index of the current wave being played (starts at 1).
playerCurrency integer The total amount of in-game currency the player possesses.
unlockedShips array of strings A list of the unique IDs of all ships the player has unlocked.
equippedShipId string The ID of the ship the player currently has equipped.
playerMaxHealth integer The maximum health value the player's ship can have.
playerCurrentHealth integer The current health value of the player's ship.
adReviveAvailable boolean Flag indicating if the player can use the ad revive.
adReviveCooldown float The time in seconds until the ad revive is available again.

2.2 Ship Data

Defines the properties of each ship available to the player.

Field Name Type Description
shipId string A unique identifier for the ship (e.g., "ship_basic", "ship_premium_01").
name string The display name of the ship.
description string A short description of the ship's role or characteristics.
baseHealth integer The maximum health of the ship.
baseDamage integer The base damage output of the ship.
baseAttackSpeed float The base time in seconds between attacks.
isPremium boolean True if the ship is a paid IAP item, false otherwise.
priceCurrency integer The amount of in-game currency required to unlock (if not premium).
priceRealMoney float The real-money price of the ship (if premium).

2.3 Upgrade Data

Defines the available upgrades for each ship.

Field Name Type Description
upgradeId string A unique identifier for the upgrade.
shipId string The ID of the ship this upgrade applies to.
name string The display name of the upgrade.
description string A description of the upgrade's effect.
costCurrency integer The amount of in-game currency required to purchase.
effectType string The type of bonus provided (e.g., "health", "damage", "attackSpeed").
effectValue float The magnitude of the bonus provided.

2.4 Enemy Data

Defines the properties of each enemy type.

Field Name Type Description
enemyId string A unique identifier for the enemy.
name string The display name of the enemy.
health integer The total health of the enemy.
damage integer The damage the enemy deals per attack.
attackSpeed float The time in seconds between enemy attacks.
movementSpeed float The speed at which the enemy travels towards the player.
weakness string The type of damage the enemy is weak against (e.g., "energy", "kinetic").
resistance string The type of damage the enemy is resistant to.

3. Core Systems

3.1 Game State Machine

A central state machine that manages the flow of the game (e.g., Main Menu, In-Game, Game Over, Wave Complete, Shop).

3.2 Combat System

Manages the automated battle between the player's ship and waves of enemies, including the Rock-Paper-Scissors damage matrix.

3.3 Upgrade System

Allows players to spend currency to purchase upgrades for their ships.

3.4 Monetization System

Integrates Unity Ads and Unity IAP to provide the specified monetization features.

4. Monetization Logic

4.1 Rewarded Ad - Revive

  • Trigger: Player's ship health reaches 0.
  • Action: Presents a UI prompt to watch a rewarded ad.
  • Success: If the player watches the full ad, playerCurrentHealth is set to playerMaxHealth * 0.5. adReviveAvailable is set to false, and a cooldown timer begins. The 'Game Over' screen is dismissed.
  • Failure/Skip: The 'Game Over' screen persists.

4.2 Rewarded Ad - Currency Doubling

  • Trigger: Player completes a wave.
  • Action: Presents a UI prompt to watch a rewarded ad to double the wave's currency reward.
  • Success: If the player watches the full ad, the standard currency reward for that wave is doubled before being added to playerCurrency.

4.3 In-App Purchase - New Ship

  • Trigger: Player selects the new ship in the Shop/Hangar and confirms purchase.
  • Action: Initiates a transaction with Unity IAP for the specified price ($1.99).
  • Success: Upon successful payment confirmation from the store, the shipId for the new ship is added to the unlockedShips array in the GameStateManager. The player is granted the ship immediately.

Initial setup for future co-op multiplayer architecture.

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-001 Scenario 1: Player revives after ship death using a rewarded ad Given the player's ship has just been destroyed When the player chooses to watch a rewarded ad Then the player's ship should be instantly revived at 50% health, and the ad should be marked as watched to prevent immediate reuse.

US-002 Scenario 2: Player doubles currency after completing a wave using a rewarded ad Given the player has just successfully completed a wave When the player chooses to watch a rewarded ad Then the player's currency reward for that wave should be doubled, and the ad should be marked as watched.

US-003 Scenario 3: Player purchases the new ship design Given the player is on the main menu When the player navigates to the IAP store and purchases the 'Stellar Navigator' ship for $1.99 Then the 'Stellar Navigator' ship should be permanently unlocked for the player, and the payment should be successfully processed.

US-004 Scenario 4: Player selects the newly purchased ship Given the 'Stellar Navigator' ship has been purchased and unlocked When the player selects the 'Stellar Navigator' ship in the hangar Then the 'Stellar Navigator' ship should be equipped and ready for use in gameplay.

{ "content": "# Solar System Coop: Technical Specifications\n\n## TS-001: Rewarded Ad - Revive Mechanic\n\n### 1. Overview\nThis feature allows the player to revive their ship with 50% health after a destruction event by watching a Unity Rewarded Video Ad.\n\n### 2. System Components\n- AdManager: A central manager responsible for initializing, loading, displaying, and handling the callbacks for Unity Ads.\n- PlayerController: The player's main script, which will detect ship destruction and trigger the AdManager.\n- PlayerStats: A component on the player that manages health.\n\n### 3. Data Structures\n- AdManager Config: A configuration asset or scriptable object that holds the Ad Unit IDs for the revive feature.\n- PlayerProgression Data: The main save data object must store a boolean flag hasWatchedReviveAdToday to prevent abuse.\n\n### 4. Logic Flow\n1. Player's ship is destroyed.\n2. Player is presented with a UI option to 'Revive with Ad' or 'Respawn'.\n3. If the player selects 'Revive with Ad' and hasWatchedReviveAdToday is false:\n a. The AdManager attempts to load and display the rewarded ad.\n b. Upon successful ad completion, the AdManager calls a callback to the PlayerController.\n c. The PlayerController sets hasWatchedReviveAdToday to true.\n d. The PlayerStats component is set to 50% of its maximum health.\n e. The game resumes from the point of destruction.\n4. If the player selects 'Respawn' or watches the ad, the game proceeds as normal.\n5. The hasWatchedReviveAdToday flag must be reset at the start of a new day (based on system time or a custom in-game day cycle).\n\n### 5. Technical Notes\n- The AdManager must handle cases where the ad fails to load or the user closes the ad early.\n- The revive must be a single-use option per destruction event.\n- The hasWatchedReviveAdToday flag must be saved and loaded correctly.\n\n## TS-002: Rewarded Ad - Currency Doubling\n\n### 1. Overview\nThis feature allows the player to double the currency reward for completing a wave by watching a Unity Rewarded Video Ad.\n\n### 2. System Components\n- AdManager: Reused from TS-001.\n- WaveManager: The manager responsible for wave progression and reward distribution.\n\n### 3. Data Structures\n- AdManager Config: Must hold the Ad Unit ID for the currency doubling feature.\n- PlayerEconomy Data: The main save data object must store a boolean flag hasUsedCurrencyDoublerThisWave to prevent abuse.\n\n### 4. Logic Flow\n1. The player successfully completes a wave.\n2. The WaveManager calculates the standard currency reward.\n3. The WaveManager presents the player with a UI option to 'Double Reward with Ad' or 'Accept Standard Reward'.\n4. If the player selects 'Double Reward with Ad' and hasUsedCurrencyDoublerThisWave is false:\n a. The AdManager attempts to load and display the rewarded ad.\n b. Upon successful ad completion, the AdManager calls a callback to the WaveManager.\n c. The WaveManager doubles the calculated reward and adds it to the player's economy.\n d. The WaveManager sets hasUsedCurrencyDoublerThisWave to true.\n e. The game proceeds to the next wave.\n5. If the player selects 'Accept Standard Reward' or watches the ad, the standard reward is applied.\n6. The hasUsedCurrencyDoublerThisWave flag must be reset at the start of the next wave.\n\n### 5. Technical Notes\n- Similar error handling as the revive ad is required.\n- The reward doubling must only apply to the current wave's completion reward.\n\n## TS-003: In-App Purchase - 'Stellar Navigator' Ship\n\n### 1. Overview\nThis feature allows players to purchase a new, unique ship for $1.99 via the Unity In-App Purchase (IAP) system.\n\n### 2. System Components\n- IAPManager: A central manager responsible for initializing, handling, and processing all IAP transactions.\n- StoreUI: The UI screen where the player can view and purchase the ship.\n- PlayerInventory: A system that manages the player's unlocked ships and items.\n\n### 3. Data Structures\n- Product Data: The IAPManager will need configuration for the product, including:\n - productId: "com.yourcompany.solarsystemcoop.ship_stellar_navigator"\n - price: 1.99\n - currency: "USD"\n - displayName: "Stellar Navigator"\n - description: "A fast and agile ship with a unique design."\n- PlayerInventory Data: The player's save data must store a list or set of owned product IDs, e.g., ownedProducts = ["com.yourcompany.solarsystemcoop.ship_stellar_navigator"].\n\n### 4. Logic Flow\n1. The player navigates to the StoreUI.\n2. The StoreUI displays the 'Stellar Navigator' ship and its price.\n3. The player taps the 'Purchase' button.\n4. The StoreUI calls the IAPManager to initiate a transaction for the specified productId.\n5. The IAPManager communicates with the Unity IAP service to open the native payment sheet.\n6. Upon successful payment confirmation from the platform:\n a. The IAPManager receives a success callback.\n b. The IAPManager adds the productId to the player's ownedProducts in the save data.\n c. The IAPManager triggers a reward for the player (e.g., unlocks the ship in the PlayerInventory).\n d. The StoreUI is updated to reflect that the ship has been purchased.\n7. Upon failure or cancellation, the IAPManager handles the error and the StoreUI remains unchanged.\n\n### 5. Technical Notes\n- The IAPManager must handle all states: initializing, fetching products, processing transactions, and handling callbacks.\n- The productId must be unique and registered on the respective app stores.\n- The server-side validation of purchases is highly recommended for security but may be out of scope for the initial MVP.\n\n## TS-004: Ship Selection and Equipping\n\n### 1. Overview\nThis feature allows the player to select and equip their unlocked ships, including the newly purchased 'Stellar Navigator'.\n\n### 2. System Components\n- HangarUI: The UI screen where the player can view and select their ships.\n- PlayerInventory: Manages the list of all unlocked ships.\n- ShipManager: A central manager that handles the currently equipped ship and its stats.\n\n### 3. Data Structures\n- ShipData Asset: A Scriptable Object or data asset for each ship, containing its stats, visuals, and other properties.\n - shipName: "Stellar Navigator"\n - price: 1.99 (or 0 if purchased)\n - isPremium: true\n - health: 120 (Example)\n - attackPower: 15 (Example)\n - speed: 1.2 (Example)\n - visuals: Path to 3D model and materials.\n- PlayerSaveData: Must store the equippedShipId (e.g., "com.yourcompany.solarsystemcoop.ship_stellar_navigator").\n\n### 4. Logic Flow\n1. The player navigates to the HangarUI.\n2. The HangarUI queries the PlayerInventory to get a list of all unlocked ships.\n3. For each unlocked ship, the HangarUI displays its visual representation and stats.\n4. The HangarUI highlights the currently equipped ship based on the PlayerSaveData.equippedShipId.\n5. The player selects a new ship from the list.\n6. The HangarUI calls the ShipManager to equip the selected ship.\n7. The ShipManager updates the PlayerSaveData.equippedShipId.\n8. The ShipManager loads the ShipData for the newly equipped ship and applies its stats to the player's current game state.\n9. The HangarUI updates to show the newly equipped ship as selected.\n\n### 5. Technical Notes\n- The ShipData assets should be designed to be easily extensible for future updates.\n- The PlayerInventory must be queried correctly to ensure only purchased or unlocked ships are displayed.\n- The ShipManager must correctly apply the stats of the newly equipped ship to the player's active stats.\n\n## TS-005: Combat Effectiveness (Rock-Paper-Scissors)\n\n### 1. Overview\nThis system defines a combat advantage/disadvantage relationship between different ship types to add strategic depth.\n\n### 2. System Components\n- ShipData: Each ship's data asset must include a combatType enum (e.g., 'Rock', 'Paper', 'Scissors').\n- CombatSystem: The core game loop logic that handles ship-to-ship interactions.\n\n### 3. Data Structures\n- ShipData.combatType: An enum or string field (e.g., 'Rock', 'Paper', 'Scissors').\n\n### 4. Logic Flow\n1. When the CombatSystem calculates damage from Ship A to Ship B:\n2. It retrieves the combatType for both Ship A and Ship B.\n3. It applies a multiplier based on their relationship:\n - If Ship A's type beats Ship B's type (e.g., Rock beats Scissors), apply a damage bonus (e.g., 1.5x).\n - If Ship B's type beats Ship A's type (e.g., Scissors beats Paper), apply a damage penalty (e.g., 0.75x).\n - If the types are the same or have no defined relationship, apply no multiplier.\n\n### 5. Technical Notes\n- The specific relationships and multipliers must be carefully balanced.\n- This system should be extensible to support more combat types in the future.\n\n## TS-006: Progression & Upgrade Matrix (Tier 1)\n\n### 1. Overview\nThis defines the structure for the player's upgrade path, focusing on the first tier of upgrades.\n\n### 2. System Components\n- UpgradeManager: Manages the player's available upgrades and the logic for purchasing them.\n- PlayerEconomy Data: Stores the player's current currency.\n- UpgradeData Asset: A Scriptable Object or data asset for each upgrade.\n\n### 3. Data Structures\n- UpgradeData:\n - upgradeId: "upgrade_attack_1"\n - displayName: "Increase Attack Power"\n - description: "Permanently increases the player's base attack power."\n - cost: 100 Currency\n - prerequisites: null (for the first tier)\n - upgradeType: "stat"\n - statToUpgrade: "attackPower"\n - valueIncrease: 5\n - maxLevel: 3\n- PlayerUpgradeData: The player's save data must store the current level for each upgrade, e.g., upgradeLevels = {"upgrade_attack_1": 0, "upgrade_health_1": 0}.\n\n### 4. Logic Flow\n1. The UpgradeManager displays available upgrades to the player.\n2. For each upgrade, it checks if the player has met the prerequisites and has enough cost.\n3. If the player purchases an upgrade:\n a. The cost is deducted from their currency.\n b. The PlayerUpgradeData.upgradeLevels for that upgrade is incremented.\n c. The UpgradeData.valueIncrease is applied to the player's base stats via the ShipManager.\n d. The upgrade's maxLevel is checked to determine if it's still available.\n\n### 5. Technical Notes\n- The PlayerUpgradeData must be saved and loaded correctly.\n- The stats applied by upgrades must be cumulative and correctly applied to the currently equipped ship.\n\n## TS-007: Enemy Compendium Data Structure\n\n### 1. Overview\nDefines the data structure for storing information about each enemy type.\n\n### 2. System Components\n- EnemyData Asset: A Scriptable Object or data asset for each enemy.\n\n### 3. Data Structures\n- EnemyData:\n - enemyName: "Basic Drone"\n - health: 50\n - attackPower: 10\n - attackSpeed: 1.0\n - speed: 5.0\n - combatType: "Paper" (Example)\n - visuals: Path to 3D model and materials.\n\n### 5. Technical Notes\n- This structure is designed to be extensible with more complex enemy attributes in the future.\n\n## TS-008: Core State Management\n\n### 1. Overview\nDefines the high-level states of the game and how they transition.\n\n### 2. System Components\n- GameManager: The central orchestrator of the game states.\n\n### 3. Data Structures\n- GameState Enum:\n - MainMenu\n - Hangar\n - Store\n - Gameplay (includes wave progression, combat, upgrades)\n - GameOver\n\n### 4. Logic Flow\nThe GameManager is responsible for loading the appropriate UI and game systems based on the current GameState and handling transitions between them (e.g., from MainMenu to Gameplay upon starting a new game).\n\n### 5. Technical Notes\n- A robust state machine is crucial for managing the game's flow and ensuring a smooth player experience.\n" }

Technical Design Document (TDD)

▼

Solar System Coop: Technical Design Overview

▼

Solar System Coop: Technical Design Overview

1. System Architecture

The game will be developed using the Unity engine. The architecture will be designed with a modular approach to support future expansion, particularly for co-op multiplayer. The core systems will manage game state, player progression, and monetization.

2. Core Systems Specifications

2.1 Game State Manager

Manages the overall game's current state and player progress.

Field Name Type Description
currentState enum The current state of the game. Possible values: MainMenu, Hangar, Store, Gameplay, GameOver.
currentWave integer The index of the current wave being played (starts at 1).
playerCurrency integer The total amount of in-game currency the player possesses.
unlockedShips List A list of the unique IDs for all ships the player has unlocked.
equippedShipId string The ID of the ship the player currently has equipped.
playerMaxHealth integer The maximum health value the player's ship can have.
playerCurrentHealth integer The current health value of the player's ship.
adReviveAvailable boolean Flag indicating if the player can use the ad revive.
adReviveCooldown float The time in seconds until the ad revive is available again.

2.2 Economy Manager

Manages all currency transactions and rewards.

Field Name Type Description
baseWaveReward int The standard amount of currency awarded for completing a wave.
doubleRewardMultiplier int The multiplier applied when a rewarded ad is watched at Wave Complete. Set to 2.

2.3 Ad Manager (Unity Ads)

This system interfaces with the Unity Ads SDK to display rewarded video ads.

Field Name Type Description
adUnitId_Revive string The specific ad unit ID for the Ship Death revive ad.
adUnitId_DoubleReward string The specific ad unit ID for the Wave Complete double reward ad.
isReviveAdReady boolean Flag to track if a revive ad is available to be shown.
isDoubleRewardAdReady boolean Flag to track if a double reward ad is available to be shown.

2.4 IAP Manager (Unity IAP)

This system interfaces with the Unity IAP SDK to handle the premium ship purchase.

Field Name Type Description
premiumShipProduct_ID string The unique product ID for the $1.99 premium ship in the store.
isPremiumShipOwned bool A flag that is set to true upon successful purchase and loaded from player data.

3. Data Structures

3.1 Ship Data Structure

Defines the properties of each ship in the game.

Field Name Type Description
shipId string A unique identifier for the ship (e.g., "ship_basic", "ship_premium_01").
name string The display name of the ship.
description string A short description of the ship's role or characteristics.
baseHealth integer The maximum health of the ship.
baseDamage integer The base damage output of the ship.
baseAttackSpeed float The base time in seconds between attacks.
movementSpeed float The ship's base movement speed.
combatType string The type of attack (e.g., "piercing", "explosive", "standard"). Used for the Combat Effectiveness matrix.
isPremium boolean Flag indicating if this ship is a paid item.
priceCurrency integer The amount of in-game currency required to unlock (if not premium).
priceRealMoney float The real-money price of the ship (if premium).
visualAssetPath string The path to the ship's 3D model and materials.

3.2 Enemy Data Structure

Defines the properties of each enemy type.

Field Name Type Description
enemyId string A unique identifier for the enemy type.
name string The display name of the enemy.
health integer The total health of the enemy.
damage integer The damage the enemy deals per attack.
attackSpeed float The time in seconds between enemy attacks.
movementSpeed float The speed at which the enemy travels towards the player.
combatType string The type of damage the enemy is weak against (e.g., "energy", "kinetic").
resistanceType string The type of damage the enemy is resistant to.
unlockWave integer The wave number at which this enemy type first appears. Defaults to 1.
visualAssetPath string The path to the enemy's 3D model and materials.

3.3 Upgrade Data Structure

Defines the available upgrades for each ship.

Field Name Type Description
upgradeId string A unique identifier for the upgrade.
shipId string The ID of the ship this upgrade applies to.
name string The display name of the upgrade.
description string A description of the upgrade's effect.
costCurrency integer The amount of in-game currency required to purchase.
effectType string The type of bonus provided (e.g., "health", "damage", "attackSpeed").
effectValue float The magnitude of the bonus provided.
maxLevel integer The maximum level this upgrade can be purchased to.

4. Monetization Flow & Logic

4.1 Rewarded Ad - Revive on Death (US-001)

  • Trigger: Player's ship health reaches zero.
  • Action: Presents a UI prompt to watch a rewarded ad. The adReviveAvailable flag must be true.
  • Success: Upon completion, playerCurrentHealth is set to 50% of playerMaxHealth. adReviveAvailable is set to false, and adReviveCooldown timer starts. The 'Game Over' screen is dismissed.
  • Failure/Skip: The 'Game Over' screen persists. adReviveAvailable remains false until the cooldown expires.

4.2 Rewarded Ad - Currency Doubling (US-002)

  • Trigger: Player successfully completes a wave.
  • Action: Presents a UI prompt to watch a rewarded ad to double the wave's currency reward. The isDoubleRewardAdReady flag must be true.
  • Success: Upon completion, the standard wave reward is doubled and added to playerCurrency. isDoubleRewardAdReady is set to false, and a short cooldown timer begins.
  • Failure/Skip: The standard, non-doubled reward is awarded. isDoubleRewardAdReady remains true.

4.3 In-App Purchase - 'Stellar Navigator' Ship (US-003)

  • Trigger: Player confirms purchase of the 'Stellar Navigator' for $1.99 in the Store.
  • Action: Initiates a transaction via the Unity IAP system.
  • Success: Upon successful payment, the isPremiumShipOwned flag is set to true, and the 'Stellar Navigator' is added to the unlockedShips list in the player's save data. The player is granted the ship immediately.
  • Failure: The transaction is cancelled, and the player's inventory remains unchanged.

5. Progression & Upgrade Logic

5.1 Unlocking New Ships

  • New ships are unlocked by meeting specific unlockWave requirements or by purchasing them via IAP.
  • The unlockedShips list in PlayerProgression Data tracks all owned ships.

5.2 Upgrading Ships

  • Players spend playerCurrency to purchase upgrades for their ships.
  • The UpgradeData table defines the cost, effect, and prerequisites for each upgrade.
  • The PlayerUpgradeData tracks the current level of each upgrade.

6. Combat Effectiveness (Rock-Paper-Scissors)

6.1 System Overview

A strategic advantage system based on matching ship and enemy combatTypes.

6.2 Logic

When a player's ship attacks an enemy:

  1. The CombatSystem compares the combatType of the attacker and defender.
  2. A multiplier is applied based on a predefined matrix (e.g., +1.5x for advantage, -0.75x for disadvantage).
  3. The final damage is calculated as (Attacker's Base Damage) * (Multiplier). The playerMaxHealth and enemyHealth are also affected by this logic.

7. Future Considerations

  • Implement robust cooldowns for rewarded ads.
  • Add more ships, enemies, and upgrade tiers.
  • Develop a robust save/load system.
  • Design and implement the co-op multiplayer architecture.

Art Bounty: SHP_001 Basic Ship (2D)

▼

Task: Create SHP_001 Basic Ship Art

Objective: Create the default, entry-level player ship for the game.

Project Context: This is the player's starting vessel, a simple and functional design that represents the foundation of their fleet. It should be visually distinct but not overly powerful compared to later ships.

Technical Specs:

  • Format: PNG sprite sheet
  • Resolution: 128x128 pixels
  • Style: Consistent with the 'Solar System Coop' art direction (clean, functional, sci-fi).
  • Content: A single sprite of a basic, single-weapon-slot ship. The design should be practical and not have any obvious special features.

Unity Import Checklist:

  1. Import the PNG into Unity.
  2. Set Texture Type to 'Sprite (2D and UI)'.
  3. Ensure Pixels Per Unit is set appropriately (e.g., 100).
  4. Create a new Prefab for the ship.
  5. Add a SpriteRenderer component and assign the imported sprite.
  6. Add a BoxCollider2D for hit detection.
  7. Create a new script (e.g., ShipController) and attach it to the prefab.

Technical Specs:

  • Format: PNG sprite sheet
  • Resolution: 64x64 pixels per frame/texture
  • Style: Clean, functional, and consistent with the ship art.
  • Content: A sprite of a standard, rapid-fire projectile. It should be a small, simple shape (e.g., a blue energy bolt or a small bullet).

Unity Import Checklist:

  1. Import the sprite sheet into Unity.
  2. Set Texture Type to 'Sprite (2D and UI)'.
  3. Ensure 'Sprite Mode' is set to 'Multiple' if using a sprite sheet.
  4. Slice the sprite sheet into individual frames (e.g., 3-4 frames for a simple animation).
  5. Create a Prefab for the projectile.
  6. Add a SpriteRenderer component and assign the first frame.
  7. Add a BoxCollider2D for hit detection.
  8. Create a new script (e.g., RapidFireWeapon) and attach it to the player ship prefab. This script will handle firing the projectile prefab at a set rate.

Bounty: VFX_006 - Basic Enemy Impact

▼

Task: Create VFX_006 - Basic Enemy Impact

1. Objective: Create a simple, clear, and performant 2D impact particle effect for when a player's weapon hits a basic enemy.

2. Project Context: This effect is a fundamental combat feedback element for the 'Solar System Coop' project. It must be visually consistent with the game's clean, sci-fi aesthetic and trigger reliably on successful hits in the 2D space.

3. Technical Specifications:

  • Format: A single, optimized 2D sprite sheet (e.g., 32x32 pixels) containing 4-6 frames of animation. The file must be a PNG with transparency.
  • Content: A small, energetic burst of light or sparks. It should be a non-intrusive but satisfying visual cue.
  • Animation: The animation should be short, snappy, and loopable for a single impact.

4. Unity Import Checklist:

  • Import the PNG into Unity.
  • Configure the texture as a Sprite (2D and UI).
  • Create a new Particle System prefab.
  • Configure the Particle System to use the imported sprite sheet for its texture.
  • Set the emission rate to 1 (for a single burst).
  • Configure the lifetime to be very short (e.g., 0.5 seconds).
  • Set the start speed to a low value (e.g., 0-5 m/s).
  • Ensure the particle system is set to 'Play on Awake' and is not looping.
  • Create a new script to trigger this particle effect from a weapon's hit detection logic.

  • Create a new HealthManager script on the player's ship.
  • Create a public function (e.g., UpdateHealthBar(float currentHealth, float maxHealth)) that calculates the fill amount and updates the foreground bar's fillAmount property.
  • Call this function whenever the player's health changes.
  • Ensure the bar is positioned clearly on the screen (e.g., top-left corner).

Implement Wave Progression with Increasing Difficulty

▼

Task: Implement Wave Progression with Increasing Difficulty

1. Overview

This task focuses on building the core game loop by implementing the wave-based progression system. The system will manage the spawning of enemies, the transition between waves, and the increasing difficulty as the player progresses.

2. Project Context

This feature is a foundational element of 'Solar System Coop', a single-player, wave-based survival defense game. The core gameplay loop revolves around defending against increasingly challenging waves of enemies on a fixed map. This task will implement the logic for managing these waves and the associated difficulty scaling.

3. User Stories

  • US-001: Wave Completion Doubled Currency
    • Scenario 1: Player completes a wave and receives double currency.
      • Given the player has 100 currency units.
      • When the player successfully defeats the final enemy of Wave 5.
      • Then the player's currency should be 200 units.
    • Scenario 2: Player completes a wave and receives standard currency.
      • Given the player has 100 currency units.
      • When the player successfully defeats the final enemy of Wave 1.
      • Then the player's currency should be 110 units.
  • US-002: Player Revives with 50% Health on Death
    • Scenario 1: Player chooses to revive after death.
      • Given the player's health is 0% after being defeated in a wave.
      • When the player watches a full rewarded video ad.
      • Then the player's health should be restored to 50% of its maximum value.
      • And the player should remain in the current wave.
    • Scenario 2: Player chooses not to revive after death.
      • Given the player's health is 0% after being defeated in a wave.
      • When the player chooses not to watch the rewarded video ad.
      • Then the player's health should remain at 0%.
      • And the game should transition to the Game Over screen.

4. Technical Specifications

  • WaveManager Script: A central script responsible for managing the current wave number, enemy spawn timers, and wave completion logic.
  • EnemyData ScriptableObject: A data asset for each enemy type, containing its stats (HP, speed, etc.) and its reward currency. The WaveManager will reference a list of these assets to determine which enemies to spawn for the current wave.
  • GameManager State: The GameManager will manage the game state, transitioning to InGame_WaveInProgress, InGame_WaveComplete, or InGame_ShipDestroyed based on player actions and events.
  • Rewarded Ad Integration: Use the Unity Ads SDK to trigger rewarded video ads for the 'Revive' and 'Double Currency' mechanics. The WaveManager will be responsible for presenting these offers at the appropriate times.
  • PlayerState Data: The PlayerState script will manage the player's currency and health. It will receive the reward amount from the WaveManager upon successful wave completion.
  • Difficulty Scaling: The WaveManager will use a configuration table (e.g., a 2D array or ScriptableObject list) to define the number and types of enemies for each wave. The number of enemies and their stats should increase with each subsequent wave.

5. Acceptance Criteria

  • The game correctly progresses from Wave 1 to Wave 2, then to Wave 3, and so on.
  • The difficulty (number and type of enemies) increases as the player progresses through the waves.
  • The 'Double Currency' ad offer appears after each wave completion, and the reward is correctly doubled upon successful viewing.
  • The 'Revive' ad offer appears upon ship destruction, and the player's ship is correctly respawned with 50% health upon successful viewing.
  • The 'Game Over' screen is correctly displayed if the player chooses not to revive.

6. Unity Import Checklist

  • Unity Ads SDK
  • Player Ship Prefab (2D)
  • Enemy Prefabs (2D)
  • PlayerState Script
  • WaveManager Script
  • GameManager Script
  • EnemyData ScriptableObjects
  • UI Prefabs for Revive/Double Currency prompts

Implement Core Economy & Progression Data

▼

Task: Implement Core Economy & Progression Data

1. Overview

This task focuses on setting up the foundational data structures and systems for the game's economy and player progression. This includes managing player currency, unlocking ships, and defining upgrade paths.

2. Project Context

This feature is central to the long-term engagement strategy of 'Solar System Coop'. The Economy Matrix is designed to provide a clear, data-driven path for player growth, ensuring a sense of accomplishment and providing hooks for monetization. This task will implement the core data assets and the initial set of upgrades and ships.

3. User Stories

  • US-001: Player Revives After Ship Death Using a Rewarded Ad
    • Scenario: Player revives after ship death using a rewarded ad.
      • Given the player's ship has been destroyed.
      • When the player watches a full rewarded ad.
      • Then the player's ship should be instantly respawned with 50% health.
      • And the player's currency should not be affected.
  • US-002: Player Doubles Currency After Completing a Wave
    • Scenario: Player doubles currency after completing a wave.
      • Given the player has just completed a wave of enemies.
      • When the player chooses to watch a rewarded video ad.
      • Then the player's currency reward for that wave should be doubled.
  • US-003: Player Purchases New Ship Design
    • Scenario: Player successfully purchases a new ship.
      • Given the player has more than $1.99 in currency.
      • When the player navigates to the Ship Customization menu and confirms the purchase of the 'Stardust Cruiser' for $1.99.
      • Then the player's currency should be reduced by $1.99.
      • And the 'Stardust Cruiser' should become available for the player to equip.

4. Technical Specifications

  • PlayerState Data Structure: A central script or data asset that persists player data. It must contain:
    • float currency
    • List<string> unlockedShips
    • string currentShipId
    • int upgradePoints
  • ShipData ScriptableObjects (2D): Data assets for each ship. Each SO must contain:
    • string shipId (e.g., 'StardustCruiser')
    • string name
    • string description
    • float baseHealth
    • float baseDamage
    • float baseAttackSpeed
    • bool isPremium (true for IAP ships)
    • string visualAssetPath (path to the 2D sprite/prefab)
  • UpgradeData ScriptableObjects (2D): Data assets for each upgrade.
    • string upgradeId (e.g., 'ship_damage_1')
    • string name
    • string description
    • int cost
    • string effectType (e.g., 'damage', 'health')
    • float effectValue
    • int requiredWave
  • GameConfiguration ScriptableObject: A central configuration asset that holds:
    • A list of all ShipData SOs.
    • A list of all UpgradeData SOs.
    • A list of all EnemyStats SOs.
    • The initial currency reward per wave.
    • The double currency multiplier.
    • The IAP product ID for the 'Stardust Cruiser' (IAP_SHIP_STARDUST).
  • Data Persistence: The PlayerState data must be saved and loaded using PlayerPrefs or a similar persistent storage solution.

5. Acceptance Criteria

  • The PlayerState data is correctly saved and loaded upon game restart.

  • The UI for purchasing the 'Stardust Cruiser' correctly displays its price and stats.
  • A player with sufficient currency can successfully purchase the 'Stardust Cruiser', and their currency is correctly decremented.
  • The 'Stardust Cruiser' is added to the unlockedShips list in PlayerState and becomes selectable in the game.
  • The UpgradeData SOs for the first tier of upgrades are correctly configured with their costs and requiredWave values.

Implement Monetization: Rewarded Ads & IAP

▼

Task: Implement Monetization: Rewarded Ads & IAP

1. Overview

This task focuses on integrating the monetization strategy for 'Solar System Coop', specifically implementing the Rewarded Video Ads and In-App Purchase (IAP) systems using Unity's official SDKs.

2. Project Context

Monetization is crucial for the long-term viability of the project. This task will implement the 'Second Chance' revive ad, the 'Double Currency' ad, and the single premium ship purchase. The goal is to provide clear value to the player for their engagement and spending.

3. User Stories

  • US-001: Player Revives After Ship Destruction Using a Rewarded Ad
    • Scenario: Player revives after ship death using a rewarded ad.
      • Given the player's ship has been destroyed.
      • When the player watches a full rewarded video ad.
      • Then the player's ship should be instantly respawned with 50% health.
      • And the player's currency should not be affected.
  • US-002: Player Doubles Currency After Completing a Wave
    • Scenario: Player doubles currency after completing a wave.
      • Given the player has just completed a wave of enemies.
      • When the player chooses to watch a rewarded video ad.
      • Then the player's currency reward for that wave should be doubled.
  • US-003: Player Purchases New Ship Design
    • Scenario: Player successfully purchases a new ship.
      • Given the player has more than $1.99 in currency.
      • When the player navigates to the Ship Customization menu and confirms the purchase of the 'Stardust Cruiser' for $1.99.
      • Then the player's currency should be reduced by $1.99.
      • And the 'Stardust Cruiser' should become available for the player to equip.

4. Technical Specifications

  • Rewarded Ads Integration (Unity Ads SDK):
    • Implement a RewardedAdManager script.
    • Configure two ad placements: AD_REVIVE_DEATH and AD_CURRENCY_DOUBLE.
    • Implement functions to request and show ads for each placement.
    • Handle ad callbacks (onLoaded, onFailed, onClosed) to trigger in-game rewards (health restore, currency boost) and manage cooldowns (e.g., 5 minutes for revive, 10 minutes for currency double).
  • In-App Purchases Integration (Unity IAP):
    • Set up the IAP product IAP_SHIP_STARDUST ($1.99) in the Unity IAP catalog.
    • Implement an IAPManager script.
    • Implement InitiatePurchase(string productId) and RestorePurchases() functions.
    • Handle transaction success, failure, and cancellation callbacks.
    • Upon successful purchase of IAP_SHIP_STARDUST, call the PlayerState to unlock the 'Stardust Cruiser' and deduct the specified currency cost.
    • Implement a PlayerPrefs or similar system to store and restore purchases.
  • Data Structures: The PlayerState and ShipData ScriptableObjects from Task TS-002 must be modified to support these features (e.g., PlayerState needs a cooldowns dictionary, ShipData needs isPremium flag).

5. Acceptance Criteria

  • The 'Revive' ad can be successfully watched, and the player's ship is restored to 50% health.
  • The 'Double Currency' ad can be successfully watched, and the player's reward for the current wave is correctly doubled.
  • The 'Stardust Cruiser' can be successfully purchased for $1.99, the player's currency is reduced, and the ship is permanently unlocked.
  • The cooldown timers for the rewarded ads are correctly implemented and enforced.
  • The IAP purchase is correctly restored if the player reinstalls the game.

6. Unity Import Checklist

  • Unity Ads SDK
  • Unity IAP SDK
  • PlayerState Script (modified)
  • ShipData ScriptableObjects (modified)
  • IAPManager Script
  • RewardedAdManager Script
  • UI Prefabs for ad prompts and the IAP store page.

Implement Combat Effectiveness (Rock-Paper-Scissors) Logic

▼

Task: Implement Combat Effectiveness (Rock-Paper-Scissors) Logic

1. Overview

This task focuses on implementing the strategic combat system where different damage types have varying effectiveness against different enemy types. This will add a layer of tactical depth to the game.

2. Project Context

This feature is a key part of the 'Solar System Coop' combat loop, as defined in the GDD. It leverages the 'Economy Matrix' concept to create a strategic 'rock-paper-scissors' dynamic that encourages players to choose the right weapons for the situation.

3. User Stories

  • US-001: Player revives after ship death using a rewarded ad
    • Scenario: Player revives after ship death using a rewarded ad.
      • Given the player's ship has been destroyed.
      • When the player watches a full rewarded video ad.
      • Then the player's ship should be instantly respawned with 50% health.
      • And the player's currency should not be affected.
  • US-002: Player doubles currency after completing a wave
    • Scenario: Player doubles currency after completing a wave.
      • Given the player has just completed a wave of enemies.
      • When the player chooses to watch a rewarded video ad.
      • Then the player's currency reward for that wave should be doubled.
  • US-003: Player purchases new ship design
    • Scenario: Player successfully purchases a new ship.
      • Given the player has more than $1.99 in currency.
      • When the player navigates to the Ship Customization menu and confirms the purchase of the 'Stardust Cruiser' for $1.99.
      • Then the player's currency should be reduced by $1.99.
      • And the 'Stardust Cruiser' should become available for the player to equip.

4. Technical Specifications

  • DamageType & ResistanceType Enums: Define enums for DamageType (e.g., Kinetic, Fire, Water, Electric) and ResistanceType (e.g., Kinetic, Bio, Water, Shields).
  • WeaponData Modification: The WeaponData ScriptableObjects must include a damageType field.
  • EnemyData Modification: The EnemyData ScriptableObjects must include weakness and resistance fields of type ResistanceType.
  • CombatSystem Logic: The main CombatSystem or WeaponManager script will be responsible for calculating damage. When a player's weapon attacks an enemy:
    1. Retrieve the damageType of the weapon and the resistance and weakness of the target enemy.
    2. Check if damageType matches the enemy's weakness. If yes, apply a weaknessMultiplier (e.g., 1.5).
    3. Check if damageType matches the enemy's resistance. If yes, apply a resistanceMultiplier (e.g., 0.5).
    4. If neither matches, use a standardMultiplier (e.g., 1.0).
    5. Calculate the final damage: weapon.baseDamage * playerShip.damageMultiplier * enemy.healthMultiplier * multiplier.
  • Configuration Table: A configuration table or script will be required to store the specific multiplier values for each DamageType vs. ResistanceType combination (e.g., Fire vs. Bio = 1.5).

5. Acceptance Criteria

  • A player using a 'Fire' weapon against a 'Bio' enemy deals 1.5x the normal damage.
  • A player using a 'Fire' weapon against a 'Water' enemy deals 0.5x the normal damage.
  • A player using a 'Kinetic' weapon against any enemy type deals standard damage (1.0x).
  • The EnemyData assets correctly define the weakness and resistance for each enemy type.

6. Unity Import Checklist

  • Player Ship Prefab (2D)
  • Enemy Prefabs (2D)
  • WeaponData ScriptableObjects (with damageType field)
  • EnemyData ScriptableObjects (with weakness and resistance fields)
  • CombatSystem Script
  • Configuration table/script for damage multipliers.

2. Project Context

A robust state management system is essential for a structured and maintainable game, as highlighted in the GDD. This will provide a clear framework for handling transitions between the main menu, in-game states, and the upgrade/store screens.

3. User Stories

  • US-001: Player revives after ship death using a rewarded ad
    • Scenario: Player revives after ship death using a rewarded ad.
      • Given the player's ship has been destroyed.
      • When the player watches a full rewarded video ad.
      • Then the player's ship should be instantly respawned with 50% health.
      • And the player's currency should not be affected.
  • US-002: Player doubles currency after completing a wave
    • Scenario: Player doubles currency after completing a wave.
      • Given the player has just completed a wave of enemies.
      • When the player chooses to watch a rewarded video ad.
      • Then the player's currency reward for that wave should be doubled.
  • US-003: Player purchases new ship design
    • Scenario: Player successfully purchases a new ship.
      • Given the player has more than $1.99 in currency.
      • When the player navigates to the Ship Customization menu and confirms the purchase of the 'Stardust Cruiser' for $1.99.
      • Then the player's currency should be reduced by $1.99.
      • And the 'Stardust Cruiser' should become available for the player to equip.

4. Technical Specifications

  • GameState Enum: Define an enum to represent the primary states of the game: public enum GameState { MainMenu, InGame_WaveInProgress, InGame_WaveComplete, InGame_ShipDestroyed, UpgradeMenu, StoreMenu }

  • GameManager Script: A central singleton script that manages the game's state machine.

    • It will hold a GameState currentState variable.
    • It will contain public functions to transition between states (e.g., GoToUpgradeMenu(), StartWave(int waveNumber)).
    • It will be responsible for initializing and de-initializing systems based on the current state (e.g., starting enemy spawners when entering InGame_WaveInProgress).

  • State Transition Logic: Implement the logic for moving between states. For example, when the player's ship is destroyed, the CombatSystem will call GameManager.Instance.TransitionToState(GameState.InGame_ShipDestroyed).

  • Data Management: The GameManager will hold references to all other major managers (e.g., WaveManager, UIManager, PlayerState, IAPManager) and pass relevant data between them.

  • Upon ship destruction, the game correctly transitions to the InGame_ShipDestroyed state and presents the revive/game over prompt.

Implement Player Revival via Rewarded Ads

▼

Task: Implement Player Revival via Rewarded Ads

1. Objective

Implement the 'Second Chance' mechanic, allowing players to revive their ship with 50% health after destruction by watching a rewarded video ad.

2. Project Context

This feature is a core part of the monetization and player retention strategy, designed to give players a second opportunity to succeed and reduce frustration from unexpected deaths. It is a key component of the 'Rewarded Advertisements' monetization pillar.

3. User Stories

US-001: Player Revives After Death

  • Given the player's ship has just been destroyed
  • When they tap the 'Revive (Watch Ad)' button on the death screen
  • And the rewarded video ad plays to completion
  • Then the player's ship should be reset at the start of the current wave with 50% health.
  • And the 'canWatchReviveAd' flag in the AdManager should be set to false for the specified cooldown period.

US-002: Player Skips Revival

  • Given the player's ship has just been destroyed
  • When they tap the 'Continue to Menu' button (or close the ad)
  • Then the 'Game Over' screen should be displayed.
  • And the player's currency should not be affected.

4. Technical Specifications

4.1. System Components

  • AdManager (Singleton): A new global service to manage all Unity Ads integration. It will be responsible for initializing the SDK, checking ad availability, showing ads, and handling callbacks.
  • DeathScreenUI: The UI panel that appears upon ship destruction. It will contain the 'Revive (Watch Ad)' and 'Continue to Menu' buttons.
  • PlayerController: Will be modified to accept a health reset event from the AdManager.

4.2. Implementation Steps

  1. Integrate Unity Ads SDK: Add the SDK to the project and configure the 'Rewarded Video' ad unit with the placement ID PlayerRevive. Ensure the AdManager initializes the SDK on game start.
  2. Create AdManager: Implement the AdManager script with functions for ShowReviveAd() and OnReviveAdComplete(bool success). This function will be called by the Unity Ads callback system.
  3. Modify DeathScreenUI: Update the 'Revive' button to call AdManager.Instance.ShowReviveAd(). Update the 'Continue' button to call SceneManager.LoadScene("MainMenu").
  4. Implement Revival Logic: In AdManager.OnReviveAdComplete(), if success is true, call a public function on the PlayerController to reset its health to 50% and place it at the start of the current wave. Also, set the canWatchReviveAd flag to false and start a timer for the cooldown.
  5. Implement Cooldown: The AdManager will manage a timer. When the timer expires, it will set canWatchReviveAd back to true and update the UI to re-enable the 'Revive' button.

5. Acceptance Criteria

  • The 'Revive' button is correctly displayed after player death.
  • Tapping 'Revive' and watching a full ad correctly restores the player's ship to 50% health at the start of the wave.
  • Tapping 'Continue' correctly transitions the player to the 'Game Over' screen.
  • The 'Revive' button is disabled for the duration of the cooldown period.

6. Unity Import Checklist

  • Unity Ads SDK Package
  • Ad Placement ID configured in Unity Ads dashboard for 'PlayerRevive'.
  • AdManager script created and attached to a global GameObject.
  • DeathScreenUI prefab updated with new button logic.
  • PlayerController script updated with a ResetHealth() function.

Implement Double Currency via Rewarded Ads

▼

Task: Implement Double Currency via Rewarded Ads

1. Objective

Implement a feature where players can optionally watch a rewarded video ad after completing a wave to double the amount of currency they earn for that wave.

2. Project Context

This feature provides an alternative to standard progression, allowing players to accelerate their resource gain by engaging with ads. It is a key component of the 'Rewarded Advertisements' monetization pillar.

3. User Stories

US-001: Player Doubles Currency After Wave Completion

  • Given the player has just completed a wave and earned 100 currency
  • When they tap the 'Double Reward (Watch Ad)' button
  • And the rewarded video ad plays to completion
  • Then the player's currency total should increase by 200 (100 base + 100 bonus).
  • And the canWatchDoubleCurrencyAd flag in the AdManager should be set to false for the specified cooldown period.

US-002: Player Skips Double Currency

  • Given the player has just completed a wave and earned 100 currency
  • When they tap the 'Standard Reward' button (or close the ad)
  • Then the player's currency total should increase by only 100.
  • And the canWatchDoubleCurrencyAd flag in the AdManager should remain true (or be reset if it was false).

4. Technical Specifications

4.1. System Components

  • AdManager (Singleton): Will manage the rewarded ad logic. It will have a new function ShowDoubleCurrencyAd(). The OnDoubleCurrencyAdComplete(bool success) callback will be implemented.
  • WaveCompleteScreenUI: The UI panel displayed after a successful wave. It will contain the 'Double Reward (Watch Ad)' and 'Standard Reward' buttons.
  • CurrencyManager: A global service that manages the player's currency. It will have a function to add currency, which will be called by the AdManager.

4.2. Implementation Steps

  1. Integrate Unity Ads SDK: Ensure the SDK is integrated and the 'Rewarded Video' ad unit with the placement ID DoubleCurrency is configured.
  2. Modify AdManager: Add the ShowDoubleCurrencyAd() function and the OnDoubleCurrencyAdComplete() callback. The callback will take the base currency reward for the wave as a parameter.
  3. Update WaveCompleteScreenUI: Update the 'Double Reward' button to call AdManager.Instance.ShowDoubleCurrencyAd(). The 'Standard Reward' button will call CurrencyManager.Instance.AddCurrency(baseReward). The UI will be hidden after a button is pressed.
  4. Implement Doubling Logic: In AdManager.OnDoubleCurrencyAdComplete(), if success is true, call CurrencyManager.Instance.AddCurrency(baseReward * 2). If success is false, call CurrencyManager.Instance.AddCurrency(baseReward). Set the canWatchDoubleCurrencyAd flag to false and start the cooldown timer.
  5. Implement Cooldown: Similar to the revive ad, the AdManager will manage a timer to re-enable canWatchDoubleCurrencyAd after a specified duration (e.g., 1 hour).

5. Acceptance Criteria

  • The 'Double Reward' button is correctly displayed after a wave is completed.
  • Selecting 'Double Reward' and watching a full ad correctly adds double the base currency to the player's total.
  • Selecting 'Standard Reward' correctly adds only the base currency to the player's total.
  • The 'Double Reward' button is disabled for the duration of the cooldown period.

6. Unity Import Checklist

  • Unity Ads SDK Package (if not already imported).
  • Ad Placement ID configured in Unity Ads dashboard for 'DoubleCurrency'.
  • AdManager script updated with new function and callback logic.
  • WaveCompleteScreenUI prefab updated with new button logic.
  • CurrencyManager script created and attached to a global GameObject.

Scope Critique

▼

Rewarded Ads - Revive Mechanic

Severity: High

Critique: The GDD clearly defines the placement and function of the revive ad but lacks specific data on its frequency and cooldown. This is crucial for balancing its impact on player progression and preventing abuse.

Suggestion: Define the exact cooldown period between revive ad opportunities (e.g., once every 3 deaths, or a 10-minute timer). Also, specify if the 50% health is a flat amount or a percentage of the maximum health. This data must be implemented and tested within the 'Monetization Integration' task.

Reasoning: A well-defined cooldown and clear revival parameters are essential to prevent the mechanic from trivializing the core challenge of the game and to ensure it remains a valuable, but not overused, option for players. This is a critical part of the monetization strategy.

Rewarded Ads - Currency Doubler

Severity: Medium

Critique: The GDD mentions the currency doubler but does not specify its frequency or any limitations. Like the revive ad, this can be overused if not properly managed.

Suggestion: Implement a daily limit on how many times a player can use the currency doubler, or a cooldown period between uses (e.g., once every 2 waves). This data must be implemented and tested within the 'Monetization Integration' task.

Reasoning: Limiting the frequency of the currency doubler prevents it from unbalancing the game's economy and ensures it remains a special reward rather than a constant exploit. This is a key part of the monetization strategy.

IAP - Premium Ship Design

Severity: High

Critique: The GDD states the ship is 'available for a flat fee of $1.99' and has 'competitive stats,' but it does not specify the exact stats or how they compare to free ships. This is vital for justifying the purchase.

Suggestion: Create a detailed comparison table in the GDD that lists the stats of the premium ship alongside the best free ship available at that point in the game. This table must be finalized and the ship's stats must be implemented and tested within the 'IAP' task.

Reasoning: Players need to understand the tangible benefits of purchasing the premium ship. Clearly defining its superior stats is essential for driving sales and justifying the $1.99 price point. This is a core part of the monetization strategy.
